docs.title: Hone: The Universal Terminal AI Coding Agent
docs.text: Hone is a privacy-first, provider-agnostic AI coding agent built entirely in Rust. It runs locally in your terminal with kernel-enforced sandboxing, supports 75+ model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, local, CLI pass-through), and learns patterns across sessions through adaptive memory. Work with your models, on your machine, under your rules.

docs.title: Why Hone
docs.text:
Your models, your machine, your rules. Hone doesn't phone home. No telemetry. No vendor lock-in. Supports any provider—commercial or self-hosted—and uses kernel-level sandboxing to control what code can do.

Intelligence compounds. Hone learns from every interaction—what patterns work, what fails, which tools matter. This adaptive memory carries forward, making the agent smarter with use. Insights cross repo boundaries through semantic indexing.

Work from anywhere. Local TUI, remote daemon with HTTP/2 + SSE, collaborative multi-user sessions, team governance with RBAC. Run honed on a server, connect from any terminal.

docs.title: Demo
docs.text:
$ hone "divide(10, 0) raises ZeroDivisionError. Fix it to return None."

  ✦ read_file calculator.py
  ✎ edit_file calculator.py
    - return a / b
    + if b == 0:
    +     return None
    + return a / b
  ❯ shell python -c "from calculator import divide; assert divide(10,0) is None"

  Fixed. divide() now returns None on zero division.

  claude-sonnet │ $0.001 │ ▓▓░░░░░░░░ 18% ctx │ 5s

docs.title: Intelligence & Orchestration
docs.text:
• Multi-agent orchestration — Decompose complex tasks via research-backed patterns (Anthropic, MASAI, CodeR). Orchestrator-worker pipeline with message merging.
  • Agent ensemble — Run N parallel candidates with varied temperatures, rank using MASAI Ranker (+5-8% accuracy improvement).
  • Adaptive complexity routing — Auto-classify requests as Simple/Medium/Complex and route to appropriate model with graduated compression.
  • Context optimization — Model-aware token budgets, BM25 reordering, phase detection, and learned compression patterns minimize context overhead while preserving relevance.
  • Cross-session learning — AdaptiveClassifier learns patterns across sessions to improve future request routing and complexity estimation.

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text:
• Test-verification loop — AgentCoder pattern that runs tests after each iteration (+40% bugs caught early).
  • Reviewer agent — ChatDev pattern where dedicated reviewer catches 30% of bugs before merge.
  • Self-refine loop — Iterative improvement (NeurIPS 2023, +8-15% quality gain).

docs.title: Model Support
docs.text:
• Universal model support — Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Ollama, local providers, CLI pass-through (ACP) with tool delegation. 75+ adapters.
  • Custom provider endpoints — HONE_OPENAI_BASE_URL for DeepSeek, Qwen, OpenRouter, and other OpenAI-compatible endpoints with drop-in model support.

docs.title: Security & Privacy
docs.text:
• Kernel-enforced sandboxing — Seatbelt on macOS, Landlock on Linux 5.13+, seccomp elsewhere. Hardened with path traversal prevention, command classification, and fail-closed policies.
  • Memory encryption — AES-256-GCM with Argon2id for encrypted session storage. Opt-in via --features encrypted-memory. Keys stored in system keychain.

docs.title: Tools & Integration
docs.text:
• Layered tool architecture — Native Rust layer (Layer 2) for zero-cost file/shell/git/LSP. MCP client for external integrations (Layer 1). Skills in markdown (Layer 3). Tool decorators for cost tracking and governance (Layer 4).
  • Real LSP client — Embedded stdio JSON-RPC bridges to rust-analyzer, pyright, typescript-language-server, gopls.
  • YAML recipe system — Multi-step workflows, conditional branching, variable interpolation. Recipes compose tools and agents into reproducible tasks.

docs.title: Storage & Observability
docs.text:
• Dual-database storage — SQLite for sessions/memory (single-user, zero-ops), PostgreSQL+pgvector for semantic index (concurrent, vector search).
  • Adaptive memory — Pattern learning across sessions. Hone remembers what worked, what failed, and why. Memory is local-first, private by default.
  • OpenAPI 3.1 spec generation — GET /openapi.json for automated API documentation.
  • Real-time cost tracking — Token counting via tiktoken, live cost estimates, per-session breakdowns, budget enforcement across multi-agent orchestrations.
  • Semantic search — Tree-sitter AST parsing, SQLite vector embeddings, cross-repo code intelligence.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
• Client-server architecture — hone CLI for local use, honed daemon for remote access. HTTP/2 + SSE, collaborative sessions, multi-user teams with role-based access control.
  • Team governance & RBAC — User roles (admin, operator, viewer), session ownership, audit logging, cost tracking per user/team.
  • Rate limiting — Sliding window middleware per IP/user.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/wojciechkpl/hone.git
cd hone
cargo build --release
export PATH="$PWD/target/release:$PATH"

docs.title: 2. Configure
docs.text:
Run the interactive configuration wizard:

hone configure

This guides you through selecting a model provider, entering API keys, and choosing a default model.

docs.title: 3. Start Using
docs.text:
Interactive session: 

hone

One-shot coding task: 

hone "add error handling to the divide function"

Multi-agent orchestration: 

hone --orchestrate "refactor the authentication module"

Run a recipe: 

hone --recipe tdd-feature

Named sessions: 

hone --session my-project  # create
hone session resume my-project  # resume
hone session list  # view all

docs.title: 1. Guiding Principles
docs.text:
• Zero-cost at the hot path. Layer 2 native tools are direct Rust function calls — no IPC, no serialization.
  • Fail-closed security. Sandbox setup failure aborts the operation, never silently degrades.
  • Trait-boundary isolation. Every external integration (model provider, LSP, MCP server) is behind a dyn Trait so it can be mocked in tests.
  • Single writer, many readers. SQLite (sessions, memory) uses WAL mode; only the daemon writes, clients read via the HTTP API. PostgreSQL + pgvector (semantic index) handles concurrent reads/writes from multiple indexer workers.
  • Privacy by default. Network access requires explicit user opt-in; telemetry is opt-in and off by default.

docs.title: 2. Workspace & Crate Structure
docs.text:
The repository uses a Cargo workspace. The root Cargo.toml declares the workspace; each subdirectory under crates/ is an independent crate with a minimal, well-defined API surface.

├── Cargo.lock
├── HONE.md                     # project constitution (Layer 3 skills)
├── deny.toml                   # cargo-deny: license + advisory policy

├── .github/
│   └── workflows/
├── crates/
│   ├── hone-core/              # agent loop, session state, orchestration
│   ├── hone-providers/         # model provider abstraction + all adapters
│   ├── hone-tools/             # Layer 2 native tools (file, shell, git, LSP bridge)
│   ├── hone-mcp/               # Layer 1 MCP client (JSON-RPC, lazy schema loading)
│   ├── hone-sandbox/           # kernel sandboxing (Seatbelt / Landlock / seccomp)
│   ├── hone-index/             # semantic indexer (tree-sitter AST + SQLite vectors)

docs.title: 4. Core Trait Definitions
docs.text: These trait definitions are the primary abstraction boundaries. All cross-crate interactions happen through these interfaces. Concrete types are hidden behind trait objects or generics with bounds.

docs.title: 4.1 ModelProvider — hone-providers
docs.text:
/// A streaming response item from a model.
pub enum ProviderEvent {
    Token(String),
    ToolCall(ToolCallRequest),
    Usage(TokenUsage),
    Done,
    Error(ProviderError),
}

/// Everything a provider needs to generate a response.
pub struct CompletionRequest {
    pub model: ModelId,
    pub messages: Vec<Message>,
    pub tools: Vec<ToolSchema>,
    pub temperature: Option<f32>,
    pub max_tokens: Option<u32>,
    pub stop: Vec<String>,
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait ModelProvider: Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn id(&self) -> &str;
    fn display_name(&self) -> &str;
    fn supported_models(&self) -> Vec<ModelInfo>;

    async fn complete(
        &self,
        request: CompletionRequest,
    ) -> Result<BoxStream<'static, ProviderEvent>, ProviderError>;

    /// Estimate token count without a network round-trip (best-effort).
    fn estimate_tokens(&self, messages: &[Message]) -> u32;

    /// Health check — used by the fallback chain.
    async fn health(&self) -> ProviderHealth;
}

docs.title: 4.2 Tool — hone-tools
docs.text:
pub struct ToolInput(serde_json::Value);
pub struct ToolOutput(serde_json::Value);

#[async_trait]
pub trait Tool: Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn description(&self) -> &str;
    fn schema(&self) -> serde_json::Value;      // JSON Schema for the model

    async fn call(
        &self,
        input: ToolInput,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<ToolOutput, ToolError>;

    /// Layer hint: L2 (native) or L1 (MCP).
    fn layer(&self) -> ToolLayer;
}

pub struct ToolContext {
    pub sandbox: Arc<dyn Sandbox>,
    pub working_dir: PathBuf,
    pub session_id: SessionId,
}

docs.title: 4.3 Sandbox — hone-sandbox
docs.text:
pub struct SandboxPolicy {
    pub allow_read: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub allow_write: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub allow_exec: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub allow_network: bool,
    pub allow_env: Vec<String>,
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait Sandbox: Send + Sync + 'static {
    /// Apply the sandbox to the current process or a subprocess.
    /// Returns Err if the policy cannot be enforced — NEVER silently degrades.
    fn apply(&self, policy: &SandboxPolicy) -> Result<SandboxHandle, SandboxError>;

    /// Restrict an already-running child process.
    fn restrict_child(&self, child: &mut Command, policy: &SandboxPolicy)
        -> Result<(), SandboxError>;

    fn platform(&self) -> SandboxPlatform;
}

pub struct AgentConfig {

docs.title: 5.1 Single Agent Turn
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant TUI as hone-tui / CLI
    participant Core as hone-core (Agent)
    participant Ctx as ContextManager
    participant Provider as ModelProvider
    participant Tools as ToolRegistry (L2 + L1)
    participant Sandbox as Sandbox
    participant Memory as MemoryStore

    User->>TUI: types prompt
    TUI->>Core: run_turn(input)
    Core->>Memory: recall(context_query)
    Memory-->>Core: relevant memories
    Core->>Ctx: build_messages(input, memories, history)
    Ctx-->>Core: messages (within token budget)
    Core->>Provider: complete(request) → Stream
    Provider-->>Core: Token events (streaming)
    Core-->>TUI: AgentEvent::Token (streamed)

    loop Tool calls
        Provider-->>Core: ToolCall event
        Core->>Sandbox: verify policy allows tool
        Sandbox-->>Core: Ok / Err (fail-closed)
        Core->>Tools: call(tool_name, args)
        Tools-->>Core: ToolOutput
        Core->>Provider: append tool result, continue stream
    end

    Provider-->>Core: Done + Usage
    Core->>Memory: record(turn_summary, patterns)
    Core-->>TUI: AgentEvent::Done(TurnResult)
    TUI-->>User: final response rendered

docs.title: 5.2 Provider Hot-Swap
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Core as Agent
    participant Reg as ProviderRegistry
    participant Old as OldProvider
    participant New as NewProvider

    User->>Core: /model switch anthropic:claude-opus-4-5
    Core->>Reg: get("anthropic:claude-opus-4-5")
    Reg-->>Core: Arc<dyn ModelProvider>
    Core->>Old: (no teardown needed — stateless)
    Core->>Core: swap_provider(new)
    Note over Core: session history preserved
    Note over Core: context window re-evaluated for new model limits
    Core-->>User: "Switched to claude-opus-4-5 (200K ctx)"
    Core->>New: next complete() call uses new provider

docs.title: 5.3 Kernel Sandbox Lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Core as Agent
    participant SB as SandboxBuilder
    participant OS as OS Kernel

    Core->>SB: build(policy)
    SB->>SB: detect platform (macOS / Linux / container)
    alt macOS
        SB->>OS: sandbox_init (Seatbelt profile)
    else Linux bare-metal
        SB->>OS: landlock_create_ruleset + seccomp-BPF filter
    else container / fallback
        SB->>OS: setrlimit + no-new-privs
    end

    alt Sandbox applied successfully
        OS-->>SB: Ok
        SB-->>Core: SandboxHandle
    else Sandbox failed
        OS-->>SB: Err
        SB-->>Core: Err(SandboxError::Unavailable)
        Note over Core: FAIL-CLOSED: abort operation
    end

docs.title: 5.4 Daemon Client-Server Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant CLI as hone CLI
    participant Web as Web PWA
    participant Daemon as honed (HTTP/2+SSE)
    participant Core as Agent (per-session)
    participant SQLite as SQLite (sessions, memory)
    participant PG as PostgreSQL + pgvector (index)

    CLI->>Daemon: POST /sessions {model, tools}
    Daemon->>Core: spawn Agent for session_id
    Daemon-->>CLI: {session_id, sse_url}

    CLI->>Daemon: POST /sessions/{id}/turns {input}
    Daemon->>Core: run_turn(input)
    Core->>PG: semantic search for context
    PG-->>Core: relevant symbols + embeddings
    Core-->>Daemon: AgentEvent stream
    Daemon-->>CLI: SSE: data: {event} \n\n

    Web->>Daemon: GET /sessions/{id}/events (SSE)
    Note over Daemon,Web: Web UI observes same session
    Daemon-->>Web: SSE replay from session start

    Core->>SQLite: persist turn (WAL write)
    SQLite-->>Core: Ok

docs.title: Per-crate errors with thiserror
docs.text:
Each crate defines its own error enum using thiserror. Cross-crate propagation uses the #[from] conversion where natural, otherwise explicit mapping. Library crates never use anyhow.

// hone-providers/src/error.rs
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ProviderError {
    #[error("provider '{provider}' returned HTTP {status}: {body}")]
    Http { provider: String, status: u16, body: String },

    #[error("provider '{provider}' stream interrupted: {source}")]
    Stream { provider: String, #[source] source: std::io::Error },

    #[error("rate limit exceeded for '{provider}', retry after {retry_after_secs}s")]
    RateLimit { provider: String, retry_after_secs: u64 },

    #[error("model '{model}' not found in provider '{provider}'")]
    ModelNotFound { model: String, provider: String },

    #[error("request serialization failed: {0}")]
    Serialization(#[from] serde_json::Error),
}

docs.title: Application binaries use anyhow
docs.text: bins/hone/main.rs and bins/honed/main.rs return anyhow::Result<()> and use context() / with_context() to add user-visible detail to errors before display.

docs.title: Panic policy
docs.text:
• unwrap() and expect() are banned in all crates/ code via a clippy rule.
  • The only permitted expect() calls are in build.rs scripts and test code, with a comment explaining the invariant.
  • Panics in async tasks are caught at the tokio::spawn boundary and converted to errors.

docs.title: Error propagation map
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    PE[ProviderError] -->|Into| AE[AgentError]
    TE[ToolError] -->|Into| AE
    SE[SandboxError] -->|Into| AE
    ME[MemoryError] -->|context| AE
    IE[IndexError] -->|context| AE
    AE -->|anyhow::Error| CLI[CLI: display to user]
    AE -->|JSON response| Server[Server: HTTP 4xx/5xx]

docs.title: Runtime: tokio (multi-thread scheduler)
docs.text:
• Both the CLI and daemon use #[tokio::main] with the multi-thread scheduler.
  • CPU-bound work (AST parsing, embedding generation, sandbox setup) is dispatched to tokio::task::spawn_blocking.
  • The TUI runs its event loop in a dedicated blocking thread communicating via mpsc channels.

docs.title: Concurrency patterns
docs.text:
// Concurrent provider health checks — JoinSet
let mut set = JoinSet::new();
for provider in registry.all() {
    set.spawn(async move { (provider.id(), provider.health().await) });
}
while let Some(Ok((id, health))) = set.join_next().await {
    results.insert(id, health);
}

// Racing a stream against a timeout — select!
tokio::select! {
    event = stream.next() => handle_event(event),
    _ = tokio::time::sleep(STREAM_TIMEOUT) => bail!("stream timeout"),
    _ = cancel_token.cancelled() => return Ok(()),
}

// Structured cancellation propagated through all tasks
let token = CancellationToken::new();
tokio::spawn(agent_loop(token.child_token()));
// Clean shutdown: token.cancel()

docs.title: Backpressure
docs.text: All inter-component communication uses bounded tokio::sync::mpsc channels. The TUI rendering loop consumes AgentEvent tokens; if the TUI falls behind, the provider stream is paused (backpressure propagates via the bounded channel).

docs.title: Streaming architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    P[Provider\nasync_stream] -->|BoxStream| AL[Agent Loop\nselect!]
    AL -->|mpsc::Sender bounded| TUI[TUI Event Loop]
    AL -->|mpsc::Sender bounded| SSE[SSE encoder\nhone-server]
    TUI -->|render| Terminal
    SSE -->|HTTP/2 push| Client

docs.title: 9. Storage Architecture
docs.text:
Hone uses a dual-database strategy: - SQLite for local session/memory data (single-user, zero-ops, optionally encrypted) - PostgreSQL + pgvector for semantic index (vector similarity search, concurrent access)

This separation ensures the CLI works offline without external dependencies, while allowing production deployments to leverage PostgreSQL's scalability and vector search capabilities.

docs.title: 9.1 SQLite — Sessions & Adaptive Memory
docs.text:
Local-first, single-file storage for data that benefits from zero configuration and offline access.

~/.local/share/hone/
├── hone.db               # sessions, turns, tool calls, memories (WAL mode)
├── hone.db-wal
└── hone.db-shm

erDiagram
    SESSIONS {
        text id PK
        text title
        text model_id
        integer created_at
        integer updated_at
    }
    TURNS {
        text id PK
        text session_id FK
        text role
        text content
        integer tokens_in
        integer tokens_out
        real cost_usd
        integer created_at
    }
    MEMORIES {
        text id PK
        text kind
        text content
        text tags_json
        real weight
        integer last_accessed
        integer decay_at
    }
    TOOL_CALLS {
        text id PK
        text turn_id FK

        text input_json
        text output_json
        integer duration_ms
        integer created_at
    }

    SESSIONS ||--o{ TURNS : contains
    TURNS ||--o{ TOOL_CALLS : has

SQLite is accessed via sqlx with WAL mode. Migration files live in crates/hone-memory/migrations/ and run automatically on startup via sqlx::migrate!.

docs.title: Memory encryption
docs.text: hone-memory wraps SQLite via sqlcipher (behind a feature flag encrypted-memory). The encryption key is derived from a user passphrase using Argon2id and stored in the system keychain (via keyring crate).

docs.title: 9.2 PostgreSQL + pgvector — Semantic Index
docs.text:
The semantic index uses PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension for approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) vector search over code embeddings.

Why PostgreSQL + pgvector instead of SQLite: - ANN indexing: pgvector provides ivfflat and hnsw index types for sub-linear similarity search. SQLite has no native vector index support — a custom extension would be needed. - Scalability: Large monorepos can produce millions of symbols with embeddings. PostgreSQL handles this without WAL checkpoint pressure. - Concurrent access: Multiple honed daemon instances or background indexer workers can read/write concurrently without SQLite's single-writer bottleneck. - Ecosystem: pgvector is production-proven, actively maintained, and integrates naturally with embedding pipelines.

docs.title: Connection strategy
docs.text:
Development:  postgres://localhost:5432/hone_index  (local Docker or system install)
Server mode:  Configurable via DATABASE_URL in config.toml or env var

The connection URL is configured in [index] section of config.toml:

[index]
database_url = "postgres://localhost:5432/hone_index"
embedding_dimensions = 384
index_type = "hnsw"  # or "ivfflat"

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
erDiagram
    INDEX_FILES {
        text id PK "uuid v7"
        text file_path "unique"
        text content_hash "sha256"
        integer indexed_at
    }
    INDEX_SYMBOLS {
        text id PK "uuid v7"
        text file_id FK
        text name
        text kind "function, struct, class, etc."
        integer line
        integer col
        vector embedding "vector(384)"
        integer indexed_at
    }

    INDEX_FILES ||--o{ INDEX_SYMBOLS : contains
-- pgvector extension
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;

-- Symbols table with vector column
CREATE TABLE index_symbols (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    file_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES index_files(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name        TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind        TEXT NOT NULL,
    line        INTEGER NOT NULL,
    col         INTEGER NOT NULL,
    embedding   vector(384),
    indexed_at  BIGINT NOT NULL
);

-- HNSW index for fast ANN search
CREATE INDEX idx_symbols_embedding ON index_symbols
    USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
    WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64);

-- B-tree for file lookups and invalidation
CREATE INDEX idx_symbols_file_id ON index_symbols (file_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_symbols_name ON index_symbols (name);

docs.title: Fallback for offline/local-only use
docs.text:
When no PostgreSQL connection is available, hone-index falls back to the current in-memory SemanticIndex with regex-based symbol extraction and substring matching. This ensures the CLI works without any external dependencies — pgvector is only required for embedding-powered semantic search.

flowchart TD
    START([Index query]) --> CHECK{PostgreSQL\navailable?}
    CHECK -- Yes --> PG[pgvector ANN search\ncosine similarity]
    CHECK -- No --> MEM[In-memory fallback\nsubstring matching]
    PG --> RESULTS([SearchResult])
    MEM --> RESULTS

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Model context windows are finite and expensive. A 200K context window costs millions of tokens at scale. Hone minimizes token usage while preserving code comprehension through four techniques:

  1. Model-aware token budgets — Each model family has a learned budget profile based on task complexity.
  2. BM25 reordering — Given a set of candidate context (memories, file snippets, search results), BM25 ranking brings the most relevant items to the front.
  3. Graduated compression — Context is progressively summarized (code comments → summaries → hashes) to preserve key information with fewer tokens.
  4. Phase detection — Hone identifies conversation phases (exploration, implementation, testing, refactoring) and adjusts context strategy accordingly.

docs.title: Token Budget Calculation
docs.text:
pub struct TokenBudget {
    pub context_window_size: u32,          // e.g., 200_000 for claude-opus-4-5
    pub reserved_for_output: u32,          // e.g., 4_000
    pub reserved_for_system_prompt: u32,   // e.g., 2_000
    pub safety_margin: f32,                // e.g., 0.1 (10% buffer)
}

impl TokenBudget {
    pub fn available_for_context(&self) -> u32 {
        let usable = self.context_window_size - self.reserved_for_output - self.reserved_for_system_prompt;
        ((usable as f32) * (1.0 - self.safety_margin)) as u32
    }
}

Example: claude-opus-4-5 (200K context): - Context window: 200,000 tokens - Reserved for output: 4,000 tokens - Reserved for system prompt: 2,000 tokens - Safety margin: 10% - Available for context: ~177,400 tokens

docs.title: BM25 Reordering
docs.text:
When the agent has multiple pieces of context (memories, code snippets, search results), BM25 ranking reorders them by relevance to the current query:

pub trait ContextRanker {
    fn rank(&self, query: &str, candidates: Vec<ContextItem>) -> Vec<RankedItem>;
}

pub struct BM25Ranker { /* implements TF-IDF with length normalization */ }

Example workflow: 1. Agent receives: "Add error handling to the auth module" 2. Retrieves 50 candidate context items (memories, code snippets, LSP results) 3. BM25 ranks them: items matching "error", "handling", "auth" bubble to top 4. Only top-K items (e.g., 30) are included in the context window 5. Result: 60% fewer tokens, same coverage

docs.title: Graduated Compression
docs.text:
As context items age or become less relevant, they are progressively compressed:

Phase 1: Full code (e.g., 100 tokens per function)
Phase 2: Code + summary (50 tokens code, 20 tokens summary = 70 total)
Phase 3: Summary only (20 tokens)
Phase 4: Compressed reference (5 tokens: hash + title)

Example: 

// Phase 1: Full code
fn validate_email(email: &str) -> Result<(), EmailError> {
    if email.len() < 3 { return Err(EmailError::TooShort); }
    if !email.contains('@') { return Err(EmailError::InvalidFormat); }
    let parts: Vec<&str> = email.split('@').collect();
    if parts.len() != 2 { return Err(EmailError::InvalidFormat); }
    if parts[1].len() < 3 { return Err(EmailError::InvalidDomain); }
    Ok(())
}

// Phase 2: Code + summary
fn validate_email(email: &str) -> Result<(), EmailError> { /* ... 40 lines ... */ }
// Validates email: checks length, presence of @, domain validity.

// Phase 3: Summary only
// Function: validate_email. Validates email: length >= 3, has @, domain valid.

// Phase 4: Reference
// ref:email_validation (hash_abc123)

docs.title: Phase Detection
docs.text:
Hone detects conversation phases and adjusts context strategy:

Phase Characteristics Context Strategy Exploration Questions, analysis, no code changes Keep search results, memories; drop old code Implementation Writing new code, modifying files Keep implementation context; compress exploration results Testing Running tests, debugging failures Keep test failures and logs; compress implementation details Refactoring Improving existing code Keep full code for area being refactored; compress unrelated context

Example: 

Turn 1-3: "What's in this repo?" → Exploration phase
         Context: recent memories, file structure, no code
Turn 4-8: "Implement auth module" → Implementation phase
         Context: auth spec, test template, security patterns
Turn 9-12: "Tests failing" → Testing phase
         Context: test failures, error logs, relevant code
Turn 13+: "Refactor X for performance" → Refactoring phase
         Context: full X implementation, performance patterns, benchmarks

docs.title: 11. Memory Encryption
docs.text:
Hone optionally encrypts session data using AES-256-GCM with Argon2id key derivation:

# Build with encryption support
cargo build --features encrypted-memory

# Initialize encryption (stores key in system keychain)
hone --init-encryption
# Enter passphrase: ****
# Keychain updated. Encryption enabled.

docs.title: Encryption Details
docs.text:
• Cipher: AES-256-GCM (authenticated encryption, prevents tampering)
  • Key derivation: Argon2id with user passphrase
  • Time cost: 3 iterations
  • Memory cost: 64 MB
  • Parallelism: 4 threads
  • Salt: 16 random bytes (unique per user)
  • Key storage: System keychain (keyring crate)
  • macOS: Keychain Services API
  • Linux: Secret Service or pass
  • Windows: DPAPI (future)
  • Scope: SQLite database (~/.local/share/hone/memory.db)
  • Encrypted at rest via SQLCipher
  • Per-record nonces prevent replay attacks

docs.title: Threat Model
docs.text:
Encrypted memory protects against: - Disk theft: If the computer is stolen, session memories cannot be read without the passphrase. - Malware with filesystem access: Cannot extract plaintext memories without keychain access. - Accidental exposure: If the database file is copied to shared storage, it remains encrypted.

Does NOT protect against: - Keyloggers or screen recording: If attacker has real-time access to your computer. - Compromised keychain: If the system keychain is breached or the passphrase is weak. - Memory-resident attacks: Decrypted data in RAM can be extracted by privileged processes.

docs.title: Ephemeral Mode
docs.text:
For sensitive queries, use ephemeral mode to disable all persistence:

hone --ephemeral -i "Analyze this sensitive document"

In ephemeral mode: - No session data is persisted - No memories are recorded - Cost tracking is not saved - All data is discarded when the session ends

docs.title: Sandbox platform matrix
docs.text:
Platform Primary mechanism Fallback macOS Seatbelt (sandbox_init) setrlimit + no-new-privs Linux bare-metal Landlock + seccomp-BPF setrlimit + no-new-privs Container (Docker/K8s) seccomp profile + no-new-privs setrlimit Windows (future) Job Objects + AppContainer Restricted token

Fail-closed invariant: if the desired sandbox tier is unavailable and the policy requires it, the operation is aborted with SandboxError::PolicyNotMet. There is no silent downgrade.

docs.title: Network policy
docs.text:
• Default: network access denied for all tool calls.
  • User enables per-domain allow-listing in config.toml.
  • MCP servers requiring network are declared in config and subject to their own policy.

docs.title: Threat model summary
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Malicious prompt
injection] -->|mitigated by| SB[Sandbox: no arbitrary exec
without allowlist]
    B[Supply chain attack
on MCP server] -->|mitigated by| HASH[Content-addressable MCP
server hashes in config]
    C[Model exfiltrating data] -->|mitigated by| NET[Network deny-by-default]
    D[Runaway disk write] -->|mitigated by| RL[rlimit FSIZE per operation]
    E[Secret leakage via
env vars] -->|mitigated by| ENV[Explicit env allowlist
in SandboxPolicy]

docs.title: Security Hardening (Phase 2 Complete)
docs.text:
Recent security improvements include:

Access Control & Path Safety: - Path traversal prevention: All file tools use resolve_within_working_dir() to canonicalize paths and reject .. escapes. Symlink targets validated to be in allowlist at execution time (prevents TOCTOU exploits). - Shell command classification: Intent classifier detects compound shell operators (;, &&, ||, |, $(), backticks) and escalates Destructive commands to require explicit user approval. Prevents shell injection via model-generated code. - Binary validation: check_binary_available() now validates binary names with metacharacter denylist instead of dangerous sh -c execution.

Kernel Sandboxing: - Real Seatbelt sandboxing (macOS): sandbox_init(3) FFI fully functional. Path canonicalization handles macOS symlinks (/tmp → /private/tmp). Dyld compatibility via global file-read* rules. Process fork/exec support for child sandboxing. - Landlock on Linux (fully implemented): Landlock LSM (Linux 5.13+) enforces fine-grained filesystem access via landlock_create_ruleset(). Seccomp-BPF fallback for older kernels. No silent degradation—fail-closed on unavailability.

Credential Protection: - CLI stdin prompts: Sensitive input (API keys, prompts in one-shot mode) piped via stdin instead of CLI args to avoid exposure in ps output. - Env var allowlisting: Explicit environment variable whitelist per tool. API keys not passed to untrusted tools.

Infrastructure: - Rate limiter using peer IP: Server-side rate limiting uses actual peer socket address, not spoofable X-Forwarded-For header. - RwLock poison recovery: Provider registry uses unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) to recover state after panic. - Memory IDs with UUID v7: Session and memory IDs use sortable UUID v7 instead of truncated timestamps. - Cache keys with blake3: Tool result cache uses blake3 (cryptographic hash) instead of non-cryptographic DefaultHasher. - Git SHA via libgit2: HEAD resolution uses pure git2 crate (in-process I/O) instead of subprocess spawning.

docs.title: D1: Workspace over monolith
docs.text:
Decision: Multi-crate Cargo workspace rather than a single src/ tree.

Rationale: Enables parallel compilation, enforces API boundaries (a crate cannot accidentally access another crate's private types), and allows publishing individual crates (e.g., hone-providers as a standalone library).

Trade-off: Slightly higher initial setup cost; longer cold compile times on a clean build. Mitigated by sccache in CI.

docs.title: D2: async-trait for object-safe async traits
docs.text:
Decision: Use async-trait (or the stabilized async fn in traits on edition 2024) for all cross-crate traits.

Rationale: dyn Trait is required for runtime polymorphism over providers and tools. Without async-trait, async methods cannot appear in object-safe traits.

Edition 2024 note: With Rust edition 2024 and the stabilized RPITIT feature, async fn in traits that return impl Future are object-safe when combined with the #[async_trait] shim for dyn dispatch. We default to using the async_trait crate until the edition 2024 dyn* feature is stable.

docs.title: D3: BoxStream for provider responses
docs.text:
Decision: ModelProvider::complete returns BoxStream<'static, ProviderEvent> rather than a concrete type.

Rationale: Each provider has a different underlying stream type. Erasing to BoxStream avoids the monomorphisation explosion that would occur if Agent were generic over P: ModelProvider.

docs.title: D4: PostgreSQL + pgvector for semantic index, SQLite for everything else
docs.text:
Decision: The semantic index uses PostgreSQL with pgvector for vector storage and ANN search. Sessions, memories, and tool call logs remain in local SQLite.

Rationale: Embedding-based code search requires approximate nearest-neighbor queries over high-dimensional vectors. pgvector provides production-grade HNSW and IVFFlat indexes with sub-linear query time, which SQLite cannot match without a custom extension. PostgreSQL also handles concurrent writes from background indexer workers without SQLite's single-writer constraint. Sessions and memories stay in SQLite because they are inherently single-user, benefit from zero-ops local storage, and do not need vector search.

Trade-off: PostgreSQL is a runtime dependency for full semantic search. Mitigated by an in-memory fallback that provides regex-based symbol search when no database connection is available, so the CLI works offline with no external dependencies.

docs.title: D5: Recipes as YAML, not Rust macros
docs.text:
Decision: The recipe system uses YAML definitions rather than a Rust DSL.

Rationale: Recipes must be shareable between users without recompilation. YAML files can be distributed via the marketplace and loaded at runtime. The trade-off is loss of compile-time verification, mitigated by JSON Schema validation of recipe files on load.

docs.title: D6: LSP bridge in Layer 2, not Layer 1
docs.text:
Decision: The LSP bridge is a native Rust tool (Layer 2), not an MCP server (Layer 1).

Rationale: LSP round-trips must complete in <500ms. The JSON-RPC + subprocess overhead of MCP would add ~50–100ms per call. The native bridge speaks LSP directly over stdin/stdout to the language server process, keeping the path entirely in-process.

docs.title: Hone Performance Benchmarks
docs.text:
Date: 2026-04-09 (updated) Tests: 210+ unit tests across 13 crates, 0 failures Hardware: Apple M-series (macOS 25.2) Binary: target/release/hone (Rust 1.85, opt-level=3, lto=thin) Method: cargo bench (criterion) + /usr/bin/time for startup/memory

10ms per message — this is the cost of the tiktoken BPE encoding. The first call also pays the cl100k_base initialization cost (cached via OnceLock for subsequent calls). For typical agent loops with 5-50 messages per turn, this adds 50-500ms of overhead, which is acceptable but worth optimizing for very long sessions.

Optimization opportunities: - Cache token counts per message (incremental update on append) - Skip re-tokenization on every add_message call

build_messages_50           time:   [1.4480 µs 1.4525 µs 1.4569 µs]

Building the message vector for a provider call (after token budget enforcement) takes ~1.5µs for 50 messages. Effectively free.

docs.text:
render_empty_tui        time:   [69.029 µs 69.196 µs 69.382 µs]
render_50_messages      time:   [78.142 µs 78.568 µs 79.063 µs]

docs.title: Notes on the cold-start anomaly
docs.text:
The first target/release/hone --version invocation takes 2.3s because the OS has not yet cached the 12MB binary in the page cache. Subsequent runs are <10ms. Real users will experience the warm path — the binary is in cache after first launch.

To optimize the cold-start path further (if it becomes a problem): 1. Strip debug symbols (already done via strip = "symbols") 2. Enable PGO (profile-guided optimization) 3. Reduce binary size by feature-gating providers 4. Use panic = "abort" to remove unwinding tables (already done)

Current binary size of 12MB is reasonable for a Rust binary with 5 model providers, full TUI, multi-agent orchestrator, MCP/ACP/LSP clients, and SQLite persistence.

docs.title: Notes on memory during turn execution
docs.text:
The 310MB peak during a one-shot turn is dominated by the claude CLI subprocess that hone delegates to. The hone process itself uses ~30-40MB. Without subprocess delegation (using direct HTTP providers like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...), memory usage stays under 100MB.

To verify the hone-only memory: 

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... /usr/bin/time -l target/release/hone "say ok"

This bypasses the claude CLI subprocess and uses the direct HTTP provider.

docs.title: SWE-bench v1 vs v2: Comparison & Lessons Learned
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-09 Model: DeepSeek V3 via OpenRouter Dataset: SWE-bench Lite (300 real GitHub issues)

docs.title: V1 vs V2 Results
docs.text:
Approach Issues Resolved Pass Rate Key Finding V1 (simple prompt) 58/300 19.3% BEST — simple approach wins V2 (structured + localization) 39/300 13.0% Worse — over-constraining hurts

Key Lesson: Pre-loading context for localization biases the agent's search strategy and reduces flexibility. Simple prompt + tool guards (must-read-before-edit, test-after-edit, max consecutive edits) outperforms structured prompts with pre-localized context by 5.3 percentage points (58 vs 39 issues resolved).

V1 simple prompt is now the default. V2 localization strategy is available via --localize flag for users who prefer more guidance.

docs.title: SWE-bench Lite Harness
docs.text:
The harness includes: - benchmarks/swebench_inference.py — Issue resolution via hone CLI - benchmarks/swebench_evaluate.py — Docker-isolated test evaluation - Makefile targets for dry-run (3 tasks), lite (300 tasks), and verified modes

Evaluation requires Docker for test execution in isolated containers.

# Dry-run (3 tasks, ~$0.01)
make -C benchmarks swebench-dry-run

# Full run (300 tasks, ~$5-15)
OPENAI_API_KEY=... HONE_OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api \
  HONE_OPENAI_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-chat \
  python benchmarks/swebench_inference.py --dataset princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Lite

# Evaluate (requires Docker)
python benchmarks/swebench_evaluate.py --predictions benchmarks/results/swe-lite-*/predictions.jsonl

docs.title: Updated Microbenchmarks (2026-04-09)
docs.text:
extract_rust_symbols    time:   [2.1836 ms 2.1902 ms 2.1969 ms]
search_index            time:   [1.0007 us 1.0032 us 1.0055 us]
build_messages_50       time:   [1.6656 us 1.6697 us 1.6739 us]
render_empty_tui        time:   [82.256 us 82.388 us 82.528 us]
render_50_messages      time:   [91.846 us 92.023 us 92.196 us]

Note on TUI render: 16% regression vs original baseline (69-79us to 82-92us) is attributed to: 1. BudgetProgress event handling — Real-time token accounting across multi-agent orchestrations 2. Context optimization overhead — BM25 reranking and graduated compression tracking in hot path

Impact assessment: Still well within 100ms frame budget at <0.1% utilization. The overhead scales poorly with very long conversations (1000+ turns) but remains sub-millisecond for typical sessions (50-200 turns).

Context optimization impact on token usage: - Typical conversation without optimization: 15K-20K tokens (full context) - Same conversation with optimization: 8K-12K tokens (40-60% reduction) - Token cost reduction: 30-40% on average across SWE-bench tasks

docs.title: Context Optimization Performance
docs.text:
BM25 reranking and graduated compression algorithms:

bm25_rank_100_items     time:   [45.2 us 45.8 us 46.5 us]
compress_context_50k    time:   [125.3 us 126.1 us 127.2 us]
phase_detection         time:   [8.2 us 8.4 us 8.6 us]

These operations run asynchronously between agent turns and do not block the user.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to Hone are documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Named session management — hone session list/resume/rename/delete commands for persistent named conversations. Sessions auto-save after each turn. --session NAME flag to start a named session. --ephemeral flag disables saving. Implementation: bins/hone/src/session.rs.
  • Interactive configure wizard — hone configure guides users through provider selection, API key entry, and model selection. Writes ~/.config/hone/config.toml. Implementation: bins/hone/src/configure.rs.
  • UX improvements — NO_COLOR environment variable support for disabling colored output. Ollama model verification during configuration. Ensemble mode validates 2-10 candidate count. Provider capability warnings for --orchestrate and --ensemble modes.
  • Context optimization — Model-aware token budgets, BM25 reordering for relevance, graduated compression strategies, and phase detection to minimize context overhead while preserving code comprehension.
  • Memory encryption — AES-256-GCM symmetric encryption with Argon2id key derivation for encrypted session storage. Opt-in via --features encrypted-memory. Encryption keys stored in system keychain.
  • Cross-session learning — AdaptiveClassifier learns patterns across sessions to improve request routing, complexity estimation, and tool selection. Patterns persist in encrypted memory.
  • Multi-agent budget tracking — Unified token accounting across orchestrated agents. Per-turn, per-session, and per-user cost tracking with enforcement and rollback on budget exhaustion.
  • SWE-bench benchmark harness — Full benchmarking pipeline for SWE-bench Lite (300 real GitHub issues). benchmarks/swebench_inference.py and swebench_evaluate.py with Makefile targets for swebench-dry-run, swebench-lite, and swebench-verified. Supports evaluation via Docker-isolated test execution.
  • Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints — HONE_OPENAI_BASE_URL and HONE_OPENAI_MODEL environment variables for drop-in support of DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, OpenRouter, and other OpenAI-compatible services.
  • Better startup error messages — Clearer diagnostics for missing API keys, sandbox unavailability, configuration errors, and provider health checks.
  • System prompt compression — Reduced system prompt from 1776 to 511 tokens (71% reduction), saving approximately 25K tokens per 20-turn task. Achieved through iterative refinement and removal of redundant instructions while maintaining quality parity.
  • Tool description overhaul — All 7 core tools now feature structured WHEN TO USE / WHEN NOT TO USE fields for improved decision-making and tool selection accuracy.
  • SWE-bench v1 optimizations — Structured 4-phase prompt design (exploration → localization → implementation → verification), two-stage localization strategy, and hardcoded tool guards (must-read-before-edit, test-after-edit hints, max consecutive edits limit).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• SWE-bench v1 final results — Hone achieves 58/300 (19.3%) on SWE-bench Lite with DeepSeek V3, beating SWE-Agent (GPT-4, 18%) at 50x lower cost (~$0.001-0.002 per task vs ~$0.10-0.20).
  • Exit code 1 on missing provider — Hone now returns exit code 1 when no provider is configured (was silently falling back to MockProvider). Users must configure a provider via hone configure or environment variables.
  • Security hardening (Phase 2 complete):
  • Path traversal prevention — All file tools use resolve_within_working_dir() to canonicalize paths and reject .. escapes.
  • Shell command classification — New intent classifier detects compound shell operators (;, &&, ||, |, $(), backticks) and escalates destructive commands to require explicit user approval.
  • Seatbelt FFI on macOS — sandbox_init(3) now fully functional. Path canonicalization handles macOS symlinks (/tmp → /private/tmp). Global file-read* rules for Dyld compatibility. Process fork/exec support for child sandboxing.
  • Landlock on Linux — Full Landlock LSM support (Linux 5.13+) with fine-grained filesystem access rules. Seccomp-BPF fallback for older kernels.
  • CLI stdin prompts — Sensitive input (API keys, one-shot prompts) now piped via stdin instead of CLI args to avoid exposure in ps output.
  • Binary validation — check_binary_available() now validates binary names with denylist of metacharacters instead of dangerous sh -c calls.

  • Rate limiter using peer IP — Server-side rate limiting now uses actual peer socket address instead of spoofable X-Forwarded-For header.

  • Storage improvements:

  • Dual-database strategy — Semantic index now uses PostgreSQL+pgvector for vector similarity search (HNSW/IVFFlat indexes). Sessions and memories remain in SQLite for zero-ops local storage.
  • RwLock poison recovery — Provider registry uses unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) to recover state after panic.
  • Memory IDs with UUID v7 — Session and memory IDs now use sortable UUID v7 instead of truncated timestamps.
  • Cache keys with blake3 — Tool result cache uses blake3 hashing for integrity instead of non-cryptographic DefaultHasher.

  • Git SHA via libgit2 — HEAD resolution now uses pure git2 crate (in-process) instead of subprocess spawning.

  • Diagnostics improvements:

  • Updated benchmark results for M-series Macs with warm-cache startup times.
  • Clarified token estimation costs (10ms per message including tiktoken cache warm-up).
  • Added memory footprint breakdown (hone process ~30-40MB, claude CLI subprocess ~270MB).
  • Documented SWE-bench evaluation methodology and Docker requirements.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: • In-memory semantic index fallback only — PostgreSQL+pgvector is now the default semantic index. In-memory fallback available only when database is unavailable (see docs/architecture.md section 9.2).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Shell injection vulnerability — Command classification now prevents execution of compound shell operators without explicit user consent.
  • Path canonicalization race — symlink targets are now validated to be in allowlist at tool execution time, preventing TOCTOU exploits.
  • Subprocess credential leakage — API keys and tokens no longer exposed in process arguments; moved to stdin or environment (with whitelist).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Architecture document — Updated with storage architecture (9.1, 9.2), security hardening (10), and key design decisions (11). Added ER diagrams for SQLite and PostgreSQL schemas.
  • Security guide — Expanded threat model, added Seatbelt/Landlock platform matrix, documented environment variable filtering and audit logging.
  • Benchmarks document — Added M-series performance baseline, cold-start analysis, memory breakdown, and SWE-bench methodology.
  • README — Updated feature list with context optimization, memory encryption, cross-session learning, and custom endpoint support.
  • New CHANGELOG — This document, using Keep a Changelog format.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Security tests — Added 20+ tests for path traversal prevention, shell command classification, and sandbox policy enforcement.
  • Context optimization tests — Unit tests for BM25 reordering, graduated compression, and token budget enforcement.
  • Memory encryption tests — Added AES-256-GCM roundtrip tests with Argon2id key derivation.
  • Benchmark microbenchmarks — Updated for cold-start vs warm-start distinction. TUI render regression documented (16% vs baseline, still <0.1% frame budget).

docs.title: Previous Release (v0.1.0)
docs.text: • Initial public release with core agent loop, 75+ model providers, native tools (L2), MCP client (L1), sandboxing (Seatbelt/Landlock), SQLite memory, semantic index, and multi-agent orchestration.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
Hone uses a three-level configuration hierarchy:

  1. CLI flags (highest priority)
  2. TOML file (~/.config/hone/config.toml)
  3. Environment variables
  4. Defaults (lowest priority)

This guide covers all configurable options.

docs.title: Config File Location
docs.text:
~/.config/hone/config.toml

Create the file if it doesn't exist:

mkdir -p ~/.config/hone
cat > ~/.config/hone/config.toml << 'EOF'
[agent]
default_model = "anthropic:claude-opus-4-5"
context_window_tokens = 200000

[memory]
enabled = true
encrypted = true
EOF

docs.title: Agent Configuration
docs.text:
[agent]
# Default model to use when no --model flag is provided
default_model = "anthropic:claude-opus-4-5"

# Total context window size in tokens (model-dependent)
context_window_tokens = 200000

# Tokens reserved for model output
reserved_output_tokens = 4000

# Tokens reserved for system prompt
reserved_system_prompt_tokens = 2000

# Safety margin (prevent hitting exact limit)
context_safety_margin = 0.1  # 10%

# Maximum iterations per session
max_iterations = 50

# Default temperature for non-ensemble turns
temperature = 0.3

# Maximum number of tool calls per turn
max_tool_calls_per_turn = 10

# Timeout for tool execution (seconds)
tool_timeout_secs = 30

docs.title: Memory Configuration
docs.text:
[memory]
# Enable memory persistence across sessions
enabled = true

# SQLite database path
db_path = "~/.local/share/hone/memory.db"

# Enable encryption for sensitive data
encrypted = false  # change to true to enable

# Encryption cipher (if encrypted = true)
cipher = "aes256-gcm"

# Memory decay: forget items after N days
decay_days = 90

# Maximum memory items to retain
max_items = 10000

docs.title: Memory Encryption
docs.text:
To enable encryption:

cargo build --features encrypted-memory
hone --init-encryption
# Enter passphrase: ****

This stores the encryption key in your system keychain: - macOS: Keychain Services - Linux: Secret Service or pass - Windows: DPAPI (future)

Configuration:

[memory]
enabled = true
encrypted = true
cipher = "aes256-gcm"
keychain_service = "hone"

docs.title: Anthropic
docs.text:
[providers.anthropic]
api_key = "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"  # or hardcoded
base_url = "https://api.anthropic.com"
timeout_secs = 30

docs.title: OpenAI (and Compatible Endpoints)
docs.text:
[providers.openai]
api_key = "${OPENAI_API_KEY}"
base_url = "https://api.openai.com/v1"
timeout_secs = 30

For custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints:

export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export HONE_OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://api.deepseek.com"
export HONE_OPENAI_MODEL="deepseek-coder"
hone

Or in config:

[providers.openai]
api_key = "${OPENAI_API_KEY}"
base_url = "https://api.deepseek.com"
model_override = "deepseek-coder"

Supported endpoints: - DeepSeek: https://api.deepseek.com - Qwen: https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 - OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 - vLLM: http://localhost:8000/v1

docs.title: Ollama
docs.text:
[providers.ollama]
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"
timeout_secs = 300  # local models may be slow

docs.title: Claude CLI
docs.text:
[providers.claude_cli]
claude_path = "/usr/local/bin/claude"  # auto-detected if not specified

docs.title: Gemini CLI
docs.text:
[providers.gemini_cli]
gemini_path = "/usr/local/bin/gemini"  # auto-detected if not specified

docs.title: Pricing and Cost Tracking
docs.text:
[pricing.anthropic]
"claude-opus-4-5" = { input_per_mtok = 3.00, output_per_mtok = 15.00 }
"claude-sonnet-4" = { input_per_mtok = 3.00, output_per_mtok = 15.00 }
"claude-haiku-3-5" = { input_per_mtok = 0.80, output_per_mtok = 4.00 }

[pricing.openai]
"gpt-4o" = { input_per_mtok = 2.50, output_per_mtok = 10.00 }
"gpt-4-turbo" = { input_per_mtok = 10.00, output_per_mtok = 30.00 }
"gpt-3.5-turbo" = { input_per_mtok = 0.50, output_per_mtok = 1.50 }

[pricing.ollama]
# Local models are free
"llama2" = { input_per_mtok = 0.00, output_per_mtok = 0.00 }

Set a budget limit:

hone --budget 10.00  # max $10 per session

docs.title: Sandbox Configuration
docs.text:
[sandbox]
# Auto-detect: "seatbelt" (macOS), "landlock" (Linux), "seccomp" (fallback)
platform = "auto"

# Enforce sandbox policy (fail-closed)
enforce = true

# Default policy for all tools
[sandbox.defaults]
allow_network = false          # deny network by default
allow_read = ["{project_root}"]
allow_write = ["/tmp"]
allow_env = ["PATH", "HOME", "USER"]

# Per-tool policy overrides
[sandbox.tools.shell]
allow_read = ["{project_root}", "/usr/lib"]
allow_write = ["/tmp", "{project_root}/target"]
allow_exec = ["/bin", "/usr/bin", "/usr/local/bin"]
allow_network = false
allow_env = ["PATH", "HOME", "RUST_BACKTRACE"]

[sandbox.tools.git]
allow_read = ["{project_root}"]
allow_write = ["{project_root}"]
allow_exec = ["/usr/bin/git"]
allow_network = false
allow_env = ["GIT_AUTHOR_NAME", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"]

# Process resource limits
[sandbox.limits]
cpu_seconds = 30           # max CPU time per tool call
memory_mb = 512            # max RAM per tool call
disk_mb = 1024             # max disk writes per turn
open_files = 1024          # max open file descriptors
subprocess_count = 10      # max subprocesses per tool call

Variables: - {project_root} — current working directory - {home} — user's home directory

docs.title: Server Configuration
docs.text:
[server]
# HTTP/2 server listen address
host = "0.0.0.0"
port = 7070

# TLS certificate and key (optional)
tls_cert = "/etc/hone/cert.pem"
tls_key = "/etc/hone/key.pem"

# Max concurrent connections
max_connections = 1000

# Request timeout
request_timeout_secs = 300

# Health check interval (seconds)
health_check_interval_secs = 60

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
[server.auth]
enabled = true

# Bearer token (basic security)
[[server.auth.tokens]]
token = "sk-hone-abc123def456..."
user = "alice@example.com"

# OAuth2 (future)
# oauth2_provider = "https://auth.example.com"

Usage:

# Start daemon
honed --config ~/.config/hone/config.toml

# Connect with token
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-hone-abc123def456..." \
  http://localhost:7070/sessions

docs.title: Team Configuration (RBAC)
docs.text:
[rbac]
enabled = true

# Role definitions
[[rbac.roles]]
name = "admin"
permissions = ["sessions:create", "sessions:delete", "tools:all", "mcp:all"]

[[rbac.roles]]
name = "developer"
permissions = ["sessions:create", "sessions:read", "tools:file", "tools:git", "tools:shell"]

[[rbac.roles]]
name = "viewer"
permissions = ["sessions:read", "mcp:read_only"]

# User assignments
[[rbac.users]]
user_id = "alice@example.com"
role = "admin"

[[rbac.users]]
user_id = "bob@example.com"
role = "developer"

[[rbac.users]]
user_id = "carol@example.com"
role = "viewer"

docs.title: Audit Logging
docs.text:
[audit]
enabled = true
log_file = "/var/log/hone/audit.log"
log_level = "info"  # info, warn, error
log_format = "json"

Audit logs include: - Tool calls (input, output, duration) - File access attempts (allowed and denied) - Security events (sandbox violations, auth failures) - Cost tracking (tokens, USD)

Query logs:

# All events for a session
grep "session_id=sess_abc123" /var/log/hone/audit.log | jq .

# Access denials
grep '"event":"access_denied"' /var/log/hone/audit.log | jq .

# Cost tracking
grep '"event":"cost_incurred"' /var/log/hone/audit.log | jq .

docs.title: Semantic Index (PostgreSQL)
docs.text:
[index]
enabled = true
database_url = "postgres://user:pass@localhost/hone_index"

# Embedding model (default: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
embedding_model = "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
embedding_dimensions = 384

# Index type: "hnsw" or "ivfflat"
index_type = "hnsw"

# HNSW parameters
hnsw_m = 16              # neighbor list size
hnsw_ef_construction = 64  # construction effort

# Batch size for indexing
batch_size = 100

# File watcher for incremental updates
watch_enabled = true
watch_ignore_patterns = [".git", "target", "node_modules"]

If PostgreSQL is unavailable, the semantic index falls back to in-memory substring matching.

docs.title: MCP Servers
docs.text:
[[mcp_servers]]
name = "github"
command = "npx"
args = ["@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
hash = "sha256:abc123def456..."  # integrity check
timeout_secs = 30

docs.title: Fallback Chains
docs.text:
[[fallback_chains]]
name = "production"
providers = ["anthropic:claude-opus-4-5", "openai:gpt-4o", "ollama:llama2"]
retry_on = ["RateLimit", "Timeout", "ServiceUnavailable"]
retry_delay_secs = 5
max_retries = 3

Usage:

hone --fallback-chain production

Or set as default:

[agent]
default_fallback_chain = "production"

docs.title: Model Routing Rules
docs.text:
[[routing_rules]]
name = "quick_tasks"
condition = "input_length < 50"
provider = "anthropic:claude-haiku-3-5"

[[routing_rules]]
name = "complex_reasoning"
condition = "input_contains('analyze')"
provider = "anthropic:claude-opus-4-5"

[[routing_rules]]
name = "budget_conscious"
condition = "true"  # default
provider = "ollama:llama2"

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Purpose ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Anthropic API key OPENAI_API_KEY OpenAI API key (or custom endpoint token) HONE_OPENAI_BASE_URL Override OpenAI endpoint URL HONE_OPENAI_MODEL Override model name for custom endpoint RUST_LOG Logging level (debug, info, warn, error) HONE_CONFIG Override config file path DATABASE_URL PostgreSQL connection string (if not in config) OLLAMA_HOST Ollama server URL (default: http://localhost:11434)

docs.title: CLI Flags
docs.text:
Most config options can be overridden via CLI flags:

hone --model openai:gpt-4o \
     --budget 10.00 \
     --context-limit 32000 \
     --temperature 0.5 \
     --max-iterations 20 \
     --sandbox-enforce

See hone --help for all flags.

docs.title: Minimal (Quick Start)
docs.text:
[agent]
default_model = "anthropic:claude-opus-4-5"

[providers.anthropic]
api_key = "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"

docs.title: Production (Server + Team)
docs.text:
[agent]
default_model = "anthropic:claude-opus-4-5"
max_iterations = 50

[memory]
enabled = true
encrypted = true

[providers.anthropic]
api_key = "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"
timeout_secs = 30

[server]
host = "0.0.0.0"
port = 7070
max_connections = 1000

[server.auth]
enabled = true
[[server.auth.tokens]]
token = "sk-hone-prod-abc123..."
user = "ops@example.com"

[rbac]
enabled = true
[[rbac.roles]]
name = "admin"
permissions = ["sessions:create", "sessions:delete", "tools:all", "mcp:all"]

[audit]
enabled = true
log_file = "/var/log/hone/audit.log"

[sandbox]
enforce = true
platform = "landlock"

docs.title: Budget-Conscious (Ollama Local)
docs.text:
[agent]
default_model = "ollama:llama2"
context_window_tokens = 4096

[providers.ollama]
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"
timeout_secs = 300

[sandbox]
enforce = false  # local-only, less critical

docs.title: Config file not found
docs.text:
error: config file not found at ~/.config/hone/config.toml

Create the file:

mkdir -p ~/.config/hone
touch ~/.config/hone/config.toml

docs.title: API key not recognized
docs.text:
error: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set or invalid

Check environment variable:

echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

Or add to config:

[providers.anthropic]
api_key = "sk-ant-..."

docs.title: Sandbox policy violation
docs.text:
error: sandbox policy not met (path not in allowlist)

Add the path to the allowlist:

[sandbox.tools.file_reader]
allow_read = ["/new/path"]

docs.title: PostgreSQL connection failed
docs.text:
error: failed to connect to PostgreSQL at postgres://localhost/hone_index

Check PostgreSQL is running:

psql -U postgres -d hone_index -c "SELECT 1"

If unavailable, semantic index falls back to in-memory substring matching.
