docs.title: Hone PRD Gap Analysis
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-05 Codebase snapshot: commit 9082a32 (Initial commit), branch main Total test count: 403 passing, 0 failing

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: The Hone codebase is approximately 25-30% complete against the PRD. The workspace structure is well-organized across 12 crates and 2 binaries, and foundational types, traits, and module boundaries are in place. However, the project is largely a scaffolding pass: most subsystems have trait definitions and in-memory/mock implementations but lack real integration with external systems. The CLI can stream text from Claude CLI or Gemini CLI through a functional TUI, but it cannot execute tools, run recipes, enforce sandboxing, connect to LSP servers, or persist memory. Of the 20 PRD requirements, zero are fully complete, roughly 8 are partial/stub, and 12 are missing or purely planned. The project is pre-alpha and not usable as a daily driver.

docs.title: 2. Requirements Scorecard
docs.text: Req Description PRD Priority Status Score Notes R1 75+ LLM providers P0 5 adapters exist (Claude CLI, Gemini CLI, Mock, + Anthropic/OpenAI/Ollama as todo!() stubs) STUB Only CLI pass-through providers work. Anthropic HTTP, OpenAI HTTP, and Ollama adapters are todo!(). No Bedrock, Azure, vLLM, llama.cpp, OpenRouter, or custom OpenAI-compatible. Router and fallback chain types exist but are untested with real providers. Actual count: 2 working providers, not 75+. R2 Kernel-enforced sandboxing (Seatbelt/Landlock) P0 Seatbelt profile generation works; apply() and restrict_child() are stubs that log but do nothing STUB Profile string is generated correctly. No actual sandbox_init(3) or sandbox-exec call. Landlock module exists on Linux (not verified). Container sandbox and NullSandbox exist as fallbacks. Fail-closed design is partially implemented (errors on empty profile). R3 LSP integration with 20+ language servers P0 LspBridge trait defined. MockLspBridge exists. No real LSP JSON-RPC client. STUB Language detection for 8 languages exists. AutoFixLoop logic is implemented against the trait. LspDiagnosticsTool, LspHoverTool, LspCodeActionTool wrappers exist. But there is no code that spawns an actual language server or speaks JSON-RPC. Zero real LSP integration. R4 Layered tool architecture (Native + MCP + Code Mode + Skills) P0 Native tools partially implemented. MCP client is trait + mock. Code Mode runner exists. Skills = HONE.md parser. PARTIAL Layer 2 (Native): File tools (read/write/edit/glob), shell tool, git tools (status/diff/commit/branch/checkout/undo/redo/auto-commit) exist as types. ToolRegistry and ToolDispatcher route calls. Layer 1 (MCP): McpClient trait, MockMcpClient, SchemaCache, McpTool wrapper -- all plumbing, no real MCP JSON-RPC transport. Layer 0 (Code Mode): CodeModeRunner can write a script to a temp file and execute it in a subprocess with sandbox policy. Layer 3 (Skills): HoneMd parser works. The architecture is sound but untested end-to-end because the main binary does not wire tools into the agent loop. R5 Client-server architecture with HTTP/SSE API P0 honed binary runs an Axum server with session CRUD, health, auth middleware, SSE encoder, tunnel routes, governance routes, collaborative routes. PARTIAL Server starts and serves routes. Session management is in-memory. SSE event encoding works. But there is no actual agent execution on the server side -- sessions are just metadata. No model completion flow through the server. The server is a shell waiting for an agent engine to be plugged in. R6 Local-first adaptive memory system P0 MemoryStore trait, InMemoryStore, Memory/MemoryQuery/MemoryFilter types, decay logic. STUB Types and in-memory implementation exist with record/recall/forget/decay/export/import. No SQLite persistence (sqlx is a workspace dep but unused in hone-memory). No integration with the agent loop. No pattern learning. No cross-session persistence. R7 Rust CLI/TUI with sub-100ms startup and streaming P0 TUI is functional with ratatui. Streaming tokens from Claude/Gemini CLI works. Conversation history maintained. Slash commands, themes, animations, syntax highlighting modules exist. PARTIAL This is the most complete feature. The TUI renders, accepts input, streams responses, and handles multi-turn conversations. However: no tool execution in the loop (tool calls from providers are ignored), no model switching at runtime, no cost display, no file tree panel. Startup time is likely within target given it's a compiled Rust binary. R8 HONE.md hierarchical project constitution P0 HoneMd parser in hone-config parses ## Heading sections from markdown. STUB Parser works. But there is no hierarchical loading (project + directory + user levels), no injection into agent system prompts, no runtime loading from .hone/ directories. The parser is an isolated utility with no consumers. R9 Lightweight web UI P1 No web UI code exists. MISSING No SolidJS, no frontend assets, no PWA manifest. Server routes exist but serve JSON API only. R10 YAML-based recipe system P1 Recipe types, YAML parser, RecipeRunner with step execution and test commands. 4 bundled recipes (bug-fix, code-review, refactor, tdd-feature). PARTIAL Recipe parsing and sequential execution logic is implemented. Test command validation between steps works. However, the executor is a generic closure -- no actual integration with the agent/provider system. Recipes are not accessible from the CLI (--recipe flag is accepted but ignored). R11 Real-time cost estimation P1 CostAccumulator tracks token usage and USD cost. PricingTable in hone-providers. Budget checking exists. STUB Cost accumulation math is correct and tested. But cost is not displayed in the TUI, not shown before actions, and not integrated into the agent loop. The "real-time projection before executing" feature is entirely missing. R12 Persistent incremental semantic index P1 SemanticIndex with symbol extraction (regex-based via SymbolExtractor), file indexing, search, symbol-at-position. walk_and_index for directory traversal. PARTIAL In-memory index works: can index files, search by name (exact/prefix/substring), find enclosing symbol. But: no tree-sitter integration (despite dep), no embeddings, no persistence to disk, no incremental updates via file watcher (notify dep unused), no call graph analysis. It's a basic symbol table, not a semantic index. R13 Multi-agent orchestration (lead-worker model) P1 AgentRegistry with 12 bundled agent definitions (markdown-based). AgentDef parser. STUB Agent definitions are loaded and queryable. But there is no orchestration engine, no lead-worker coordination, no parallel subagent execution. The Agent type in hone-core exists but is not wired into a multi-agent system. R14 Git-first workflow with auto-commits P1 Git tools: status, diff, commit, branch, checkout, undo, redo. AutoCommitter exists. UndoStack for tracking. PARTIAL Git tool types exist with git2 integration. Auto-committer concept is present. But none of these tools are invoked during the agent loop -- the TUI ignores tool calls. The undo/redo stack is an interesting design but has no UI surface. R15 Extension marketplace P2 No marketplace code. MISSING No discovery, installation, or registry for MCP servers or recipes. R16 Team governance: spend caps, model policies, audit logs P2 GovernanceStore with members, policies (allowed models, spend caps, approved extensions), usage tracking. Governance HTTP routes. AuditLog trait with InMemoryAuditLog. RBAC with roles and tool access control. PARTIAL Types and in-memory stores exist. HTTP routes expose CRUD for governance data. Audit log captures entries. RBAC defines roles (Admin, Developer, Viewer) with tool access. But all storage is in-memory (lost on restart), no SSO/SCIM, no real enforcement in the agent loop. R17 Cross-repository intelligence P2 MultiRepoIndex can index multiple repos and search across them. STUB The multi-repo wrapper over SemanticIndex exists and works for basic symbol search. But without real semantic analysis, embeddings, or call graphs, this is just multi-directory grep. No impact analysis across repos. R18 Test-driven editing mode P2 tdd-workflow.md agent definition bundled. tdd-feature.yaml recipe bundled. STUB An agent definition and recipe YAML exist describing the workflow. No engine to actually iterate code until tests pass. The recipe runner could theoretically drive this but is not connected to anything. R19 Voice-to-code (local Whisper) P2 No voice/audio code. MISSING No Whisper integration, no audio input handling. R20 Collaborative multi-user sessions P2 CollaborativeStore with participants, join/leave, roles (Owner/Editor/Viewer). HTTP routes. STUB Participant tracking exists in-memory. No real-time sync, no cursor sharing, no conflict resolution, no WebSocket connections. It's a participant roster, not a collaboration system.

docs.title: 3. Competitive Feature Matrix Gap
docs.text:
The PRD's competitive matrix (Section 20) makes many claims. Here is the reality check:

Claimed Advantage PRD Claim Actual Status Honest Assessment Model providers: 75+ Hone supports 75+ providers 2 working (CLI pass-through), 3 todo!() stubs FALSE. Would need to say "2 providers" today. Local models: Full Full local model support No working local model adapter (Ollama is todo!()) FALSE. Zero local model support. Kernel sandbox: Yes Kernel-enforced sandboxing Profile generation only; no enforcement FALSE. Sandbox does not enforce anything. LSP integration: 20+ langs 20+ language LSP integration Trait + mock only; 0 real LSP connections FALSE. No LSP integration exists. Tool architecture: Layered Native + MCP + Code Mode Types exist but agent loop ignores tool calls MISLEADING. Architecture is designed, not operational. Adaptive memory: Local-first Local-first adaptive memory In-memory only, no persistence, no learning FALSE. Memory is volatile and non-adaptive. Remote/mobile: PWA + Web PWA + Web UI No web UI of any kind FALSE. Client-server: Yes Full client-server Server runs but has no agent engine MISLEADING. Server is a session shell. Cost estimation: Real-time Real-time cost estimation CostAccumulator math works, not displayed FALSE. Not user-visible. Recipes/workflows: YAML YAML recipe system Parser + runner exist, not connected to CLI MISLEADING. Cannot be used in practice. Semantic index: Persistent Persistent semantic index In-memory regex symbol search, no persistence FALSE. Not persistent, not semantic (no embeddings). Git-first: Auto-commit Automatic commit per edit Tools exist, not invoked during agent execution FALSE. No auto-committing happens. Multi-agent: Lead-worker Lead-worker orchestration Agent registry only, no orchestration FALSE. Voice input: Local Whisper Local Whisper transcription No audio code FALSE. Test-driven mode: First-class First-class TDD mode Agent def + recipe YAML only FALSE. Startup time: < 100ms Sub-100ms startup Likely achievable (compiled Rust, minimal deps) PLAUSIBLE but unmeasured. Memory footprint: < 50MB Under 50MB idle Likely achievable PLAUSIBLE but unmeasured.

Bottom line: Of 17 competitive claims, approximately 2 are plausible, 3 are misleading (structure exists but doesn't function), and 12 are outright false given current implementation.

docs.title: 4. Performance Requirements Gap
docs.text:
Metric Target Current Reality Gap CLI startup time < 100ms Likely met (compiled binary, no heavy init) Low risk -- needs benchmarking to confirm First token latency (local) < 500ms No local model support at all Blocked -- Ollama adapter is todo!() First token latency (cloud) < 1.5s Depends on Claude/Gemini CLI subprocess spawn time; likely 2-4s including process start At risk -- subprocess model adds overhead vs direct HTTP Memory footprint (idle) < 50MB Likely met (no heavy allocations) Low risk -- needs profiling Memory footprint (active) < 200MB Unknown; no real workload possible yet Unknown Semantic index build (50K LOC) < 30s Regex-based extraction is fast but untested at scale; no tree-sitter Unknown -- likely met for regex, but feature is too basic Semantic index incremental < 2s No file watcher, no incremental pipeline Not applicable -- feature not built LSP diagnostic round-trip < 500ms No LSP connection Not applicable -- feature not built Session reconnect < 1s No reconnection logic Not applicable -- feature not built Web UI initial load < 500KB No web UI Not applicable -- feature not built

Summary: 2 of 10 targets are likely met (startup, idle memory). 1 is at risk (cloud latency due to subprocess model). 7 are not applicable because the features don't exist.

docs.title: Present and sound
docs.text:
• Workspace structure: Clean crate separation with clear dependency graph
  • Protocol types (hone-proto): Message, Role, Content, AgentEvent, ToolCallRequest/Result, TokenUsage, PricingEntry -- well-defined
  • Provider trait abstraction: ModelProvider trait with streaming, health checks, token estimation
  • Tool trait abstraction: Tool trait with input/output/context, ToolRegistry, ToolDispatcher
  • Sandbox trait abstraction: Sandbox trait with apply() and restrict_child(), multiple backend types
  • Config system: figment-based config loading, HoneMd parser, typed config structs

docs.title: Missing or critically incomplete
docs.text:
1. Agent execution loop: The biggest gap. The TUI streams tokens but completely ignores tool calls (ProviderEvent::ToolCall(_) => {}). There is no plan-execute-observe cycle. The agent cannot act on the codebase.

  2. Tool-calling protocol: The provider adapters (Claude CLI, Gemini CLI) do not support tool calling. The supports_tools: false flag is honest. Without tool-calling support from at least one provider, the entire tool architecture is inert.

  3. MCP transport: The McpClient trait exists but there is no JSON-RPC client implementation. No stdio or HTTP+SSE transport for MCP servers. The SchemaCache and McpTool are plumbing waiting for a transport.

  4. LSP transport: No JSON-RPC client for LSP. The entire LspBridge hierarchy operates on mocks.

  5. Persistence layer: SQLite dep is declared but unused. Memory, index, sessions, governance, audit -- all in-memory. Nothing survives a process restart.

  6. HONE.md integration: Parser exists but nothing loads HONE.md from disk, merges layers, or injects it into prompts.

  7. hone.toml routing: Config types for routing rules exist but are not connected to the ModelRouter in the provider crate.

  8. Web frontend: Entirely absent. No HTML, CSS, JS, SolidJS, or static file serving.

docs.title: 6. Critical Path to MVP
docs.text:
Ranked by user impact, with effort estimates and dependencies.

Rank Item User Impact Effort Dependencies Description 1 Agent execution loop with tool calling Blocks all agent functionality L Provider with tool support Implement the plan-execute-observe cycle: model returns tool calls, dispatcher executes them, results fed back. Without this, Hone is just a chat wrapper. 2 Anthropic HTTP provider with tool use Enables tool calling for the most capable model M None Implement the todo!() in anthropic.rs. Must support tools parameter and tool_use content blocks. Claude CLI pass-through cannot do tool calling. 3 Wire native tools into agent loop Users can edit files, run commands, do git ops M #1, #2 Register file/shell/git tools in the main binary, feed tool schemas to the provider, dispatch calls. 4 Sandbox enforcement (Seatbelt apply) Users can trust autonomous mode M None Call sandbox-exec or sandbox_init(3) in SeatbeltSandbox::restrict_child. Profile generation already works. 5 HONE.md loading and prompt injection Users can customize agent behavior per-project S #1 Load HONE.md from project root, merge with user-level, inject relevant sections into system prompt. Parser already works. 6 hone.toml config loading Users can configure models, routing, sandbox S None Wire figment-based config into main binary startup. Types exist in hone-config. 7 Cost tracking in TUI Users see what they're spending S #1, #2 CostAccumulator works. Display total cost in TUI status bar. Wire PricingTable to active model. 8 OpenAI HTTP provider Users can choose between Anthropic and OpenAI M None Implement the todo!() in openai.rs. 9 Ollama provider Users can run local models M None Implement the todo!() in ollama.rs. Critical for the "local-first" value proposition. 10 Recipe CLI integration Users can run declarative workflows M #1, #3 Connect --recipe flag to RecipeRunner. Provide an executor closure that uses the agent.

docs.title: 7. Technical Debt
docs.text:
1. CLI argument parsing is hand-rolled. The parse_args() function in main.rs manually iterates std::env::args(). Should use clap for proper arg parsing, help generation, and shell completions.

  2. DetectedProvider enum in main.rs duplicates trait dispatch. The DetectedProvider enum with manual match arms reimplements dynamic dispatch that the ModelProvider trait already provides. Should use Box<dyn ModelProvider>.

  3. No error types in main binary. Main uses anyhow::Result everywhere with no structured error handling. Provider detection, TUI setup, and agent turns should have typed errors.

  4. History accumulation is unbounded. history: Vec<Message> in the TUI loop grows without limit. No context window management, no summarization, no sliding window.

  5. In-memory everything. Every store (sessions, governance, collaborative, memory, index) is in-memory. The sqlx dependency is unused. This means zero persistence, zero crash recovery.

  6. No integration tests. All 403 tests are unit tests on isolated modules. No test starts the TUI, connects to a provider, or exercises the end-to-end flow. No integration test for the server.

  7. Provider subprocess model is fragile. Spawning claude and gemini as subprocesses and parsing their JSON output is brittle and adds latency. Should be a fallback, not the primary path.

  8. Unused dependencies. tree-sitter, sqlx, notify, keyring, argon2, tiktoken-rs, proptest, criterion are in workspace deps but appear unused or minimally used. This inflates compile times.

  9. No CI/CD pipeline visible. No GitHub Actions, no Makefile, no justfile. No automated test runs, no release builds.

  10. Seatbelt profile is never actually applied. The stub logs a debug message and returns Ok(SandboxHandle::new()). In production this would silently run without sandboxing, violating the "fail-closed" design promise.

docs.title: P0 -- Do now (blocks MVP)
docs.text:
1. Implement Anthropic HTTP provider with tool use. This unblocks the entire tool architecture. The Claude CLI pass-through cannot support tool calling, which makes every other feature dead code.

  2. Build the agent execution loop. Implement a turn-based loop: send messages + tool schemas to provider, receive tool calls, dispatch via ToolDispatcher, feed results back, repeat until Done. This is the heart of Hone.

  3. Wire native tools into the main binary. Register ReadFileTool, WriteFileTool, EditFileTool, GlobTool, ShellTool, GitStatusTool, etc. in the CLI and provide their schemas to the provider.

  4. Make Seatbelt enforcement real. Call sandbox-exec -p <profile> in restrict_child(). The profile generation already works. Without this, any tool execution in autonomous mode is unsafe.

  5. Load HONE.md and hone.toml at startup. Wire config loading so users can configure model, routing, and project conventions without editing code.

docs.title: P1 -- Do next (needed for beta)
docs.text:
1. Implement Ollama and OpenAI providers. Replace the todo!() stubs. Ollama is critical for the local-first narrative.

  2. Add SQLite persistence for memory and index. The sqlx dep is already declared. Store memories and symbol indices so they survive restarts.

  3. Build a real LSP JSON-RPC client. Start with rust-analyzer and tsserver. The trait, tools, and auto-fix loop are ready -- they just need a real transport.

  4. Display cost in TUI. The math works. Add a status bar widget showing cumulative cost and token usage.

  5. Connect recipe system to CLI. Make --recipe bug-fix actually parse the YAML, create an executor using the agent, and run the steps.

  6. Replace hand-rolled arg parsing with clap. Add subcommands: hone chat, hone recipe, hone agent, hone ext.

  7. Add context window management. Implement sliding window or summarization for conversation history before it blows the context limit.

docs.title: P2 -- Do later (nice to have)
docs.text:
1. Build web UI with SolidJS. Server routes are partially ready. Add a frontend.

  2. Implement MCP JSON-RPC transport. Enable external tool integrations (GitHub, Jira, etc.).

  3. Add multi-agent orchestration. Agent definitions are loaded. Build a lead-worker coordinator.

  4. Implement WireGuard tunnel integration. Trait and mock exist. Add a real tunnel provider.

  5. Add tree-sitter to semantic index. Replace regex symbol extraction with proper AST parsing.

  6. Set up CI/CD. GitHub Actions for test, lint, build, release.

  7. Benchmark startup time and memory. Validate the two performance claims that are plausible.

  8. SQLite-backed governance and audit. Move team governance and audit logs to persistent storage for enterprise use.

docs.title: Hone TUI Design Specification
docs.text: Version: 1.0 Date: 2026-04-05 Status: Approved for implementation

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Brand Grounding
  2. Color System
  3. Theme Presets
  4. Typography and Symbols
  5. Layout Architecture
  6. Startup Experience
  7. Conversation View
  8. Message Rendering
  9. Input Area
  10. Status Bar
  11. Tool Call Panels
  12. Split-Pane Layout
  13. Help Overlay

docs.title: 1. Brand Grounding
docs.text:
The Hone mark is a stepped, pixelated double-arrow pointing right — an abstraction of precision and forward motion. The color story runs from deep crimson (#7B1D35) through vivid rose (#E8304A) to hot pink (#F75077). The background is near-black navy (#0E1117). The tagline is "SHARPEN YOUR CODE".

These three facts drive every design decision in this spec:

  • Signature accent: the hot-pink-to-crimson gradient is Hone's identity. It must appear on exactly one element at a time — the prompt sigil, the thinking indicator, or the active border. Never diluted across multiple elements simultaneously.
  • Dark-first: the primary palette targets dark terminals. Light-terminal equivalents are defined separately in every token table.
  • Terminal-native: nothing in this spec requires sixel graphics or image rendering. Every visual element is composed from Unicode, ANSI color, and box-drawing characters alone.

docs.title: 2.1 Design Tokens
docs.text:
All colors are listed with: role, dark-terminal value (truecolor hex), 256-color ANSI approximation, and light-terminal equivalent.

Token Role Dark (hex) ANSI-256 Light (hex) ANSI-256 accent-hot Primary accent, prompt sigil #F75077 204 #C0183A 160 accent-mid Secondary accent, borders #E8304A 197 #A8102E 124 accent-deep Muted accent, decorations #7B1D35 88 #6B0D25 88 surface-base Terminal background (assume) #0E1117 233 #F5F5F0 255 surface-raised Panel, status bar fill #161B24 234 #EAEAE5 254 surface-overlay Tool call block fill #1E2535 235 #E0E0DB 253 surface-border Inactive borders #2A3347 237 #CCCCCA 251 surface-focus Active / focused border #F75077 204 #C0183A 160 text-primary Main content text #E8EAF0 252 #1A1C24 234 text-secondary Metadata, timestamps #7A8299 244 #5A5C6A 242 text-muted Disabled, placeholders #3D4456 238 #AAAAAA 248 text-on-accent Text placed on accent fill #FFFFFF 15 #FFFFFF 15 role-user User message chrome #5BA4F5 75 #1A6BC4 26 role-assistant Assistant message chrome #F75077 204 #C0183A 160 role-system System / info messages #7A8299 244 #5A5C6A 242 role-tool Tool call chrome #C084FC 177 #7E22CE 91 role-tool-result Tool result chrome #6EE7B7 120 #065F46 22 role-error Error messages #F87171 203 #B91C1C 124 syntax-keyword Code: keyword #F75077 204 #B91C1C 124 syntax-string Code: string literal #6EE7B7 120 #065F46 22 syntax-number Code: numeric literal #FCD34D 221 #92400E 130 syntax-comment Code: comment #4B5563 240 #9CA3AF 246 syntax-type Code: type / class #60A5FA 75 #1D4ED8 26 syntax-function Code: function name #C084FC 177 #7E22CE 91 diff-add Diff: added line background #052E16 22 #D1FAE5 120 diff-add-fg Diff: added line text #6EE7B7 120 #065F46 22 diff-remove Diff: removed line background #3B0A14 52 #FEE2E2 224 diff-remove-fg Diff: removed line text #F87171 203 #991B1B 124 diff-hunk Diff: hunk header #1E3A5F 18 #DBEAFE 153 diff-hunk-fg Diff: hunk header text #7A8299 244 #1E3A5F 18 budget-low Budget bar: safe zone #6EE7B7 120 #065F46 22 budget-mid Budget bar: warning zone #FCD34D 221 #92400E 130 budget-high Budget bar: danger zone #F87171 203 #B91C1C 124

docs.title: 2.2 Contrast Matrix (WCAG AA)
docs.text:
All text/background pairings used in the design must meet 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (>18pt / bold >14pt). Terminal text is treated as normal size throughout.

Foreground token Background token Ratio (dark) Ratio (light) Status text-primary on surface-base 12.1:1 10.8:1 AA pass text-secondary on surface-base 5.2:1 4.9:1 AA pass text-muted on surface-base 2.4:1 2.6:1 Decorative only — never carry meaning accent-hot on surface-base 4.6:1 4.8:1 AA pass role-user on surface-base 5.1:1 4.5:1 AA pass role-tool on surface-raised 4.7:1 4.9:1 AA pass text-on-accent on accent-hot 4.5:1 5.2:1 AA pass diff-add-fg on diff-add 5.8:1 5.6:1 AA pass diff-remove-fg on diff-remove 5.9:1 6.1:1 AA pass syntax-comment on surface-overlay 2.1:1 2.3:1 Decorative only

Note: text-muted and syntax-comment are intentionally below threshold. They are used exclusively for structural decoration (disabled hints, code comments) — never as the sole carrier of essential information.

docs.title: 3. Theme Presets
docs.text: Three named presets ship with Hone. All override only the tokens listed; unspecified tokens inherit from the default (dark) palette.

docs.title: 3.1 Default — "Crimson" (dark)
docs.text:
The primary experience. Uses the full token table from Section 2.1 as defined.

Theme name:       crimson
Background style: dark
Accent family:    red/pink (#F75077 → #7B1D35)

docs.title: 3.2 "Neon" (dark, higher contrast)
docs.text:
For high-ambient-light environments where the subdued surface colors wash out. Increases all surface-* luminance by ~15% and saturates accents.

Token override Value surface-raised #1F2937 surface-overlay #273448 surface-border #374151 accent-hot #FF2D5E role-user #38BDF8 role-assistant #FF2D5E role-tool #D946EF role-tool-result #34D399

Neon uses the same border-drawing characters but raises border brightness. The prompt sigil uses a bold modifier. All other tokens remain as Crimson.

docs.title: 3.3 "Chalk" (light)
docs.text:
For light-background terminals (e.g., macOS Terminal "Basic", iTerm "Solarized Light"). Uses the "Light" column from the contrast matrix.

Token override Value surface-base terminal default (inherit) surface-raised #EAEAE5 surface-overlay #E0E0DB surface-border #CCCCCA surface-focus #C0183A text-primary #1A1C24 text-secondary #5A5C6A text-muted #AAAAAA accent-hot #C0183A accent-mid #A8102E role-user #1A6BC4 role-assistant #C0183A role-tool #7E22CE role-tool-result #065F46

docs.title: 3.4 "Minimal" (no-color fallback)
docs.text:
When NO_COLOR is set, TERM=dumb, or the terminal reports fewer than 8 colors. All color is stripped. Visual hierarchy is achieved through:

  • Bold modifier for headers, role labels, and active borders
  • Underline for links and command names
  • Box-drawing characters for all structural borders (retained)
  • > prefix instead of colored sigil
  • [TOOL], [USER], [AI] text labels instead of colored chrome
  • Status bar rendered as plain --- separator with text fields

The Theme struct must carry a no_color: bool flag. When true, every Color::* field is replaced with Color::Reset and the renderer falls back to the Minimal layout variant.

docs.title: 4.1 Unicode Box-Drawing Characters
docs.text:
Use exclusively the standard Unicode box-drawing block (U+2500–U+257F). Do not mix single and double-line styles within the same widget.

Primary style — rounded corners (most panels): 

╭─────────────────────╮
│                     │
╰─────────────────────╯
Characters: ╭ U+256D, ╮ U+256E, ╰ U+2570, ╯ U+256F, ─ U+2500, │ U+2502

Secondary style — sharp corners (tool call blocks, diff panels): 

┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
└─────────────────────┘
Characters: ┌ U+250C, ┐ U+2510, └ U+2514, ┘ U+2518

Separator lines: 

────────────────────── (full-width horizontal, within panel)
╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌ (dashed, between messages — lighter visual weight)
Characters: ─ U+2500, ╌ U+254C

Title inset (panel headers): 

╭─ Tool: read_file ──────────────╮
The title string is inserted directly into the top border, one space padded on each side of the title text.

docs.title: 4.2 The Prompt Sigil
docs.text:
The prompt sigil is the key brand carrier in ASCII space. It must echo the stepped-arrow mark from the logo.

>

Rendered as: > in accent-hot with bold modifier, preceded by one space, followed by one space. This is the sole use of the accent color in the input area when idle.

During streaming, the sigil pulses (see Section 14).

docs.title: 4.3 Spinner Frames
docs.text:
For all thinking/loading states, use this 8-frame spinner sequence. It is compact, readable in all terminals, and has directional motion that echoes the right-pointing arrow motif:

Frame 0:  ─
Frame 1:  \
Frame 2:  │
Frame 3:  /
Frame 4:  ─
Frame 5:  \
Frame 6:  │
Frame 7:  /

Tick rate: 100ms per frame (10 fps). This is the minimum that feels smooth without burning CPU.

Alternative ASCII-safe spinner for dumb terminals: 

Frame 0:  [   ]
Frame 1:  [.  ]
Frame 2:  [.. ]
Frame 3:  [...]
Frame 4:  [ ..]
Frame 5:  [  .]

docs.title: 4.4 Progress and Sparkline Characters
docs.text:
Budget consumption sparkline uses the 8-level block fill characters: 

▁ ▂ ▃ ▄ ▅ ▆ ▇ █
U+2581 through U+2588. Each character represents one time-bucket of spend.

Inline progress bars use: 

█████░░░░░  (50%)
Fill: █ U+2588, Empty: ░ U+2591.

Thinking dots (three-dot pulse): 

   (empty pause)
.
..
...
..
.
Cycle through these 6 frames at 300ms each. Displayed immediately after the assistant sigil when streaming has not yet produced any tokens.

docs.title: 4.5 Diff Gutter Characters
docs.text:
+ added line
- removed line
  unchanged line
~ modified (context)
@ @@ hunk header

The + and - are colored with diff-add-fg and diff-remove-fg respectively. Line numbers in the gutter use text-muted.

docs.title: 5.1 Primary Layout (Single-Pane, default)
docs.text:
The terminal area is divided into four horizontal bands:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  HEADER BAR                                            1 row │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                             │
│  CONVERSATION VIEWPORT                         fills height │
│                                                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  INPUT AREA                              3–8 rows (dynamic) │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  STATUS BAR                                            1 row │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Minimum terminal size: 80 columns × 24 rows. Below this, display a single-line warning: 

Terminal too small (80×24 required). Resize to continue.

Recommended terminal size: 120 columns × 40 rows.

Height allocation: - Header bar: 1 row, fixed - Status bar: 1 row, fixed - Input area: minimum 3 rows, expands to 8 rows maximum as text wraps, then scrolls internally - Conversation viewport: all remaining rows

docs.title: 5.2 Split-Pane Layout (activated by /split or Ctrl+P)
docs.text:
┌──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
│  HEADER BAR                                           1 row  │
├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
│                              │                              │
│  CONVERSATION VIEWPORT       │  FILE PREVIEW PANEL         │
│  (left, 50% default)         │  (right, 50% default)       │
│                              │                              │
├──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┤
│  INPUT AREA                                    3–8 rows      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  STATUS BAR                                           1 row  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The split ratio is adjustable with Alt+Left / Alt+Right in 5% increments. Minimum pane width is 40 columns.

The file preview panel displays the most recently read or edited file. When a read_file or write_file tool call completes, the preview updates automatically with the file's content, syntax-highlighted, with the relevant line range scrolled into view and highlighted.

The vertical divider is: │ U+2502 in surface-border. When the preview pane has focus, the divider changes to accent-hot.

docs.title: 5.3 Tool Output Panel (bottom panel variant)
docs.text:
An alternative layout mode activated by /panel shows a three-zone layout:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  HEADER BAR                                            1 row │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                             │
│  CONVERSATION VIEWPORT                         fills height │
│                                                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  TOOL OUTPUT PANEL                              8 rows fixed │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  INPUT AREA                                    3–5 rows      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  STATUS BAR                                            1 row │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The tool output panel is a scrollable buffer showing only tool call inputs and results, separate from the conversation flow. This is useful for users who want to watch file operations without losing conversational context.

docs.title: 5.4 Column Grid
docs.text:
At different terminal widths, the layout adapts as follows:

Terminal width Layout behavior < 80 cols Warning overlay, no interaction 80–99 cols Single pane. Status bar truncates model name first, then cost. 100–119 cols Single pane. Full status bar. Input area has full width. 120–159 cols Single pane at full width, or split with 60/40 ratio. 160+ cols Split pane at 50/50, conversation viewport gets max 80 cols (centered or left-aligned per user preference).

At 160+ columns, the conversation viewport should be capped at 80 characters of content width (matching the comfort reading width for code). Excess width goes to the preview panel or left as padding.

docs.title: 6.1 Splash Screen
docs.text:
Displayed for exactly 600ms on first launch, then crossfades into the conversation view. On subsequent launches within the same working directory (detected by session file), the splash is skipped — drop directly into the conversation view with the previous session history loaded.

The splash screen occupies the full terminal and is centered both horizontally and vertically.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                             │
│                                                             │
│                                                             │
│                  >=>                                        │
│                 >==>                                        │
│                >===>   H O N E                              │
│                 >==>                                        │
│                  >=>                                        │
│                                                             │
│              sharpen your code                              │
│                                                             │
│              v1.0.0  |  rust core  |  apache 2.0            │
│                                                             │
│                                                             │
│              model: claude-sonnet-4-5                       │
│              connecting...  /                               │
│                                                             │
│                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The ASCII mark (>=> / >==> / >===>) is rendered in accent-hot (bold). "H O N E" is in text-primary (bold). "sharpen your code" is in text-secondary. Version line is text-muted. "connecting..." + spinner is text-secondary.

The mark animates on entry: the three rows appear top-to-bottom with 80ms stagger. The text "H O N E" appears letter-by-letter with 40ms stagger starting 240ms after the mark completes.

Once the model connection is established, "connecting... /" becomes "ready" in accent-hot, held for 400ms, then the transition to the conversation view begins.

docs.title: 6.2 ASCII Mark Specification
docs.text:
The stepped-arrow mark is the primary visual identity element. It must be renderable in pure ASCII across all splash, header, and no-color modes:

Full size (splash screen, 9 rows):
 >
 =>
 ==>
>==>
>===>
>==>
 ==>
 =>
 >

Colored rendering: each = character in accent-deep, each > character in accent-hot (bold).

Compact size (header bar, 1 row): 

>=>
Three characters wide. In accent-hot.

The compact mark is used in the header bar to the left of the "hone" wordmark.

docs.title: 6.3 Header Bar
docs.text:
The header bar occupies the top 1 row. It is always visible.

 >=>  hone                              ~/projects/myapp  main*

Left group: compact mark + product name. Mark in accent-hot, "hone" in text-primary bold. Right group: working directory path (shortened to last 2 path segments) and git branch (if detectable). Both in text-secondary. Background: surface-raised.

The header bar is not a Ratatui border — it is a plain Paragraph widget with manually composed content in a 1-row layout slot. This allows fine-grained color control per segment without the limitations of a border title.

docs.title: 7.1 Message Stream Layout
docs.text:
Messages render as a vertically scrollable list. Each message is a self-contained block with consistent internal structure. There is no hard line between messages — instead, vertical spacing (one blank row) acts as the separator.

For terminals narrower than 100 columns, the blank-row separator is replaced with a ╌ dashed line in text-muted.

  > hone   14:23                                              
 ╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮  
 │  Fix the token refresh race condition in auth.           │  
 ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  

  > model   14:23                                             

  I'll analyze the authentication module and fix the race      
  condition in the token refresh logic. Let me start by        
  reading the relevant files.

User message block: rounded border in role-user, role label "hone" (the product name acts as the user label, matching the > sigil), timestamp in text-muted, message body in text-primary.

Assistant message block: no border — text flows freely. Role label in role-assistant. Timestamp in text-muted. Body in text-primary. The absence of a border for assistant messages creates visual asymmetry that distinguishes them from user input and aligns with established chat conventions (border = user input, free-flow = response).

docs.title: 7.2 Role Labels
docs.text: Role Label text Color token Prefix User hone role-user (bold) > in accent-hot Assistant model (or model shortname if set) role-assistant (bold) > in role-assistant System system role-system none ToolCall tool: <name> role-tool (bold) > in role-tool ToolResult result role-tool-result none Error error role-error (bold) ! in role-error

docs.title: 7.3 Timestamp Format
docs.text: HH:MM in text-muted, right-aligned to the conversation width. On narrow terminals (< 100 cols), timestamps are omitted from the inline label and moved to a trailing position after the message body.

docs.title: 7.4 Scrolling Behavior
docs.text:
• The viewport auto-scrolls to the bottom when new content arrives.
  • Manual scroll (Page Up / Page Down, arrow keys) disengages auto-scroll.
  • A subtle scroll indicator appears in the bottom-right corner of the viewport when the user has scrolled up:
  ╰─ 12 more below ─>

Rendered in text-muted. Pressing End or G re-engages auto-scroll and dismisses the indicator.

  • Smooth scrolling is not available in Ratatui — implement instant-scroll but add a scroll_offset animation state that interpolates over 3 frames (30ms) by adjusting the rendered offset by thirds. This creates the perception of easing without true per-pixel scrolling.

docs.title: 8.1 Streaming State
docs.text:
While is_streaming: true, the assistant message renders with a thinking indicator appended to the last line of content:

Before any tokens arrive (pure thinking state): 

  > model   14:23

  ...
The three dots are text-muted. They cycle through the 6-frame dot animation (Section 4.4).

While tokens stream in: 

  > model   14:23

  I'll analyze the authentication module and fix the race
  condition. Let me start by reading the relevant files_
The cursor _ in accent-hot blinks at 500ms on / 500ms off. The cursor is appended immediately after the last character of streamed content.

After streaming completes: The cursor disappears. No other change. The message is now static.

docs.title: 8.2 Code Block Rendering
docs.text:
Fenced code blocks (``` delimited, or 4-space indented) render in a distinct container:

 ┌─ rust ─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  1  use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};                       │
 │  2                                                      │
 │  3  pub struct TokenRefresher {                         │
 │  4      token: Arc<Mutex<Option<String>>>,              │
 │  5  }                                                   │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  • Container: sharp-corner box, surface-overlay background, surface-border border.
  • Language label: inset in the top-left border in text-secondary.
  • Line numbers: right-aligned in a 4-character gutter, separated from code by one space, colored text-muted.
  • Syntax highlighting: minimal, deterministic highlighting using the syntax-* tokens. Do not depend on a tree-sitter grammar — implement a simple regex-based lexer covering: keywords, string literals, numeric literals, comments, and type names. This is sufficient for the display use case and has zero runtime cost.
  • Content: left-padded 2 spaces, right-padded 2 spaces before the border.
  • Horizontal scroll: if a line exceeds the container width, add a < / > indicator at the left/right edges and allow Alt+Left / Alt+Right to scroll the code block horizontally when it is focused.

Syntax token detection order (for the simple lexer): 1. Block comments (/* ... */) 2. Line comments (//, #, --) 3. String literals (single-quoted, double-quoted, backtick) 4. Keywords (language-specific keyword list, matched as whole words) 5. Numeric literals (\d+\.?\d*) 6. Type names (CamelCase words, or words following :) 7. Function names (word immediately preceding () 8. Default: text-primary

docs.title: 8.3 Diff Rendering
docs.text:
When a message contains a unified diff (lines starting with ---, +++, @@, +, -), the renderer switches to diff mode:

 ┌─ diff: src/auth/refresh.ts ────────────────────────────┐
 │  @@ -42,7 +42,12 @@                                    │  <- diff-hunk-fg on diff-hunk
 │    async function refreshToken() {                      │  <- unchanged
 │ -    const token = await fetchToken();                  │  <- diff-remove-fg on diff-remove
 │ +    const token = await fetchToken().catch(err => {    │  <- diff-add-fg on diff-add
 │ +      if (err.code === 'RACE_CONDITION') {             │  <- diff-add-fg on diff-add
 │ +        return retryWithBackoff(fetchToken, 3);        │  <- diff-add-fg on diff-add
 │ +      }                                                │  <- diff-add-fg on diff-add
 │ +      throw err;                                       │  <- diff-add-fg on diff-add
 │ +    });                                                │  <- diff-add-fg on diff-add
 │      return token;                                      │  <- unchanged
 │    }                                                    │  <- unchanged
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The filename is extracted from the --- a/ / +++ b/ header lines and displayed as the panel title. Hunk headers (@@) use the diff-hunk background. + lines use diff-add background for the full row width. - lines use diff-remove background for the full row width. Gutter characters (+, -, ) are bold.

A summary line appears below the diff block: 

 +6 additions  -1 deletion   src/auth/refresh.ts
Additions in diff-add-fg, deletions in diff-remove-fg, filename in text-secondary.

docs.title: 8.4 Inline Formatting
docs.text:
Markdown inline elements are rendered as follows:

Markdown Rendering **bold** Bold modifier *italic* Italic modifier (if terminal supports) `code` syntax-keyword color, no bold [link](url) Underline on link text, url in text-muted after it # Heading Bold + accent-hot, followed by ─ underline to panel width ## Heading Bold only - list item > prefix in text-muted > blockquote │ left border in text-muted, indented 2

Do not attempt to render HTML. Pass it through as literal text.

docs.title: 9.1 Normal State (Idle)
docs.text:
╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ > _                                                         │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
  Enter to send  Shift+Enter new line  / for commands  Ctrl+C quit

The border is in surface-border (inactive). The > sigil is accent-hot bold. The cursor _ blinks at 500ms. The hint line below the border is text-muted, shown only when the input buffer is empty.

docs.title: 9.2 Active Typing State
docs.text:
╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ > Fix the token refresh race condition. The issue is that   │
│   multiple concurrent calls to refreshToken() can each      │
│   trigger a fetch before any has returned, causing the tok_ │
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
  line 3 / col 54  characters: 148
  • Border changes to surface-focus (the active focus color, which is accent-hot in the default theme).
  • Lines past the first are indented 3 characters to align with the sigil offset.
  • When the input exceeds 8 rows, the box height caps at 8 rows and the content scrolls internally.
  • A character count appears bottom-left below the border in text-muted.
  • Line number and column position appear bottom-left when the input has more than one line.

docs.title: 9.3 Slash Command Autocomplete Dropdown
docs.text:
When the input buffer begins with /, an autocomplete dropdown appears above the input area:

╭─ commands ──────────────────────────────────────╮
│  /model <model-id>     switch active model      │
│  /cost                 show session cost        │
│  /undo                 undo last agent action   │
│  /redo                 redo                     │
│ [/help]                show command help        │  <- currently selected
│  /quit                 exit hone               │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ > /h_                                           │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

Dropdown behavior: - Appears immediately on / (before any further characters are typed). - Filters to matching commands as the user types. - Arrow Up / Down navigate the selection. Tab completes the current selection into the input buffer. - Enter executes the selected command. - Escape dismisses the dropdown and returns to normal input. - Selected row uses surface-overlay background and accent-hot text. - The dropdown maximum height is 10 rows. If more commands match, show a scroll indicator. - The dropdown is positioned above the input area (never below, to avoid obscuring the status bar). - Each row shows: command name in text-primary bold, arguments in text-secondary, description in text-muted.

docs.title: 9.4 Waiting State (WaitingForResponse)
docs.text:
╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│   thinking  /                                               │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
  • The input is disabled — keystrokes are absorbed but not rendered.
  • The text "thinking" is text-muted, the spinner is accent-hot.
  • The border is surface-border (same as idle — no focus indicator while waiting).
  • The hint line is replaced with: Ctrl+C to interrupt

docs.title: 9.5 Error State
docs.text:
╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ > _                                                         │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
  ! API error: rate limit exceeded. Retry in 12s.
  • Border in role-error.
  • Error message below the border in role-error.
  • Input is re-enabled so the user can retry.

docs.title: 9.6 Multi-line Paste Detection
docs.text:
When a paste event contains newlines (detected by rapid successive character events, or via Bracketed Paste Mode), the input area immediately expands to show the full pasted content up to the 8-row cap, and displays a confirmation prompt:

  Paste 6 lines?  Enter to confirm  Esc to cancel

This prevents accidental submission of large pastes.

docs.title: 10.1 Full-Width Layout (120+ columns)
docs.text:
The status bar is a single row at the bottom of the terminal.

 qwen3:32b  |  12,430 tok  |  $0.04  |  ||||||||░░  |  14:03  |  Ctrl+? help

Segments, left to right:

  1. Model name: text-primary bold. Truncated to 16 characters with … if needed.
  2. Separator: │ in text-muted
  3. Token count: formatted with commas (e.g., 12,430 tok). text-secondary.
  4. Separator: │ in text-muted
  5. Session cost: $0.04 formatted to 2 decimal places if > $0.01, 4 places if < $0.01. text-secondary. Changes to budget-mid above 50% of budget, budget-high above 80%.
  6. Separator: │ in text-muted
  7. Budget sparkline: see Section 10.2.
  8. Separator: │ in text-muted
  9. Session duration: HH:MM elapsed. Updates every minute. text-secondary.
  10. Separator: │ in text-muted
  11. Shortcut hint: Ctrl+? help in text-muted. Changes to active tool name when a tool is running (e.g., running: read_file).

Background: surface-raised. The entire status bar row has surface-raised background applied.

docs.title: 10.2 Budget Sparkline
docs.text:
The budget sparkline is a 10-character bar showing: - Cost consumption relative to the configured budget (if set). - Each character represents 10% of the budget. - Filled segments use █ (U+2588), empty segments use ░ (U+2591). - Color: budget-low from 0–50%, budget-mid from 50–80%, budget-high above 80%.

0%:    ░░░░░░░░░░
25%:   ███░░░░░░░  (budget-low)
55%:   █████░░░░░  (first segment switches to budget-mid)
85%:   █████████░  (budget-high)

When no budget is configured, display no limit in text-muted in the sparkline slot.

The sparkline is computed from session_cost_usd / budget_usd. The StatusInfo struct needs a budget_usd: Option<f64> field.

docs.title: 10.3 Narrow-Terminal Fallback (80–99 columns)
docs.text:
qwen3:32b  tok:12430  $0.04  14:03

Model name truncated to 10 characters. Cost and token count condensed. Sparkline and session duration omitted. No separator pipes — single space separators.

docs.title: 10.4 Active Tool Indicator
docs.text:
When a tool call is in progress, the status bar rightmost segment changes to:

  running: read_file  /

Where read_file is the tool name in role-tool bold, and / is the spinner in accent-hot. The spinner replaces the help hint for the duration of the tool call.

docs.title: 10.5 Mode Indicator
docs.text:
The mode field from StatusInfo (currently "chat") is displayed as a small badge to the far left of the status bar:

[CHAT]  qwen3:32b  |  ...

Badge: text-on-accent on accent-deep background. When mode is "auto" or "code", the badge color changes to accent-mid. This signals to the user which operating mode is active without requiring a separate panel.

docs.title: 11. Tool Call Panels
docs.text: Tool calls are the most complex visual element. They must communicate: what tool ran, what arguments were passed, the result, and whether it succeeded or failed — in a compact, scannable form.

docs.title: 11.1 Tool Call Block (collapsed by default)
docs.text:
┌─ > read_file ────────────────────────────────────── [+] ──┐
 │  src/auth/refresh.ts  (lines 1–89)                        │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  • Sharp-corner box, surface-overlay background.
  • Title: > sigil in role-tool, tool name in role-tool bold, [+] expand indicator in text-muted right-aligned.
  • Body: one-line summary of the arguments (file path + line range for file tools, query for search tools, etc.).
  • Press Enter (when focused) or Space to expand/collapse.

docs.title: 11.2 Tool Call Block (expanded)
docs.text:
┌─ > read_file ────────────────────────────────────── [-] ──┐
 │  Input                                                    │
 │  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
 │    path: "src/auth/refresh.ts"                            │
 │    range: [1, 89]                                         │
 │                                                           │
 │  Result                                                   │
 │  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
 │  1   import { TokenCache } from './cache';                │
 │  2   import { fetchToken } from './api';                  │
 │  3                                                        │
 │  ... (87 more lines)  Press Space to show all            │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  • Input section: argument key-value pairs, keys in text-secondary, values in text-primary.
  • Result section: truncated to 5 lines with a "N more lines" indicator. Press Space again (or e) to show the full result in a scrollable sub-view.
  • Separator lines (──) in text-muted.

docs.title: 11.3 Tool Call States
docs.text: State Visual treatment Running Title spinner in accent-hot. Box border in role-tool. Body shows "running..." in text-muted. Success [+] indicator in role-tool-result. Border surface-border. Error [!] indicator in role-error. Border role-error. Body shows error message in role-error. Approval required Border budget-mid (yellow). Body: "Approval required: {description}" with [y] yes and [n] no hints.

docs.title: 11.4 Approval Required State
docs.text:
When AgentEvent::ApprovalRequired fires, the tool call block renders in an elevated state:

 ┌─ > write_file ─────────────────────────────── [APPROVAL] ─┐
 │  This action requires your approval:                      │
 │                                                           │
 │  Write 42 lines to src/auth/refresh.ts                   │
 │                                                           │
 │  [y] Allow    [n] Deny    [d] Show diff first             │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  • Border in budget-mid (yellow — distinct from both success green and error red).
  • The block takes keyboard focus automatically. The conversation viewport loses focus.
  • y / n / d keypresses are consumed by this block.
  • [d] triggers the diff view of the proposed change in the file preview panel (split layout) or in an overlay (single layout).

docs.title: 12.1 File Preview Panel States
docs.text:
The file preview panel has its own 7 states:

Empty (no file selected): 

╭───────────────────────────────╮
│                               │

│       no file selected        │
│   tool calls will appear      │
│   here automatically          │
│                               │
│                               │

Text in text-muted, centered.

╭─ loading... ──────────────────╮

Loaded (file displayed):

│  1   use std::sync::Arc;      │
│  2   use tokio::sync::Mutex;  │
│  3                            │
│ [42] pub async fn refresh() { │  <- highlighted line
│ [43]   let guard = token      │
│  44       .lock().await;      │

╰───────────────────────────────╯
The highlighted range (from the tool call's line parameters) uses surface-overlay background on those rows. Line numbers in brackets [42] indicate the highlighted range.

Error (file not found or read error): 

╭─ error ───────────────────────╮

Above the file content. text-muted.

│   /                       open command palette             │

docs.title: 14. Animation and Motion
docs.text: All animations in Ratatui are tick-based. The event loop must call terminal.draw() on a timer tick even when no user event has occurred, to advance animation state. Recommended tick rate: 100ms (10 fps) for all spinner and typing animations.

docs.title: 14.1 Animation Registry
docs.text: Element Animation type Timing Frames / behavior Splash mark reveal Staggered row appear 80ms per row Rows top-to-bottom, each appears in full Splash wordmark reveal Letter-by-letter 40ms per letter After mark completes + 100ms delay Splash connecting state Spinner 100ms/frame 8-frame spinner (Section 4.3) Cursor blink (input) Binary toggle 500ms on / 500ms off _ shown / hidden Streaming cursor Binary toggle 500ms on / 500ms off _ in accent-hot Thinking dots (pre-token) 6-frame cycle 300ms/frame / . / .. / ... / .. / . Spinner (tool running) 8-frame cycle 100ms/frame Standard spinner Status spinner (waiting) 8-frame cycle 100ms/frame Rightmost status segment Scroll indicator fade Delayed appearance Show after 200ms of scroll position Instant on, instant off Approval block focus Border color change Instant surface-border -> budget-mid

docs.title: 14.2 Startup Sequence Timing
docs.text:
t=0ms      Terminal cleared, splash background drawn
t=80ms     First mark row appears (top '>')
t=160ms    Second mark row ('=>')
t=240ms    Third mark row ('==>')
t=320ms    Fourth mark row ('===>')
t=400ms    Fifth mark row ('==>')
t=480ms    Sixth mark row ('=>')
t=560ms    Seventh mark row ('>')
t=660ms    Wordmark 'H' appears
t=700ms    'O'
t=740ms    'N'
t=780ms    'E'
t=880ms    Tagline appears instantly
t=980ms    Version line appears
t=1080ms   Model name appears, connecting spinner starts
t=1080ms+  Wait for connection. Spinner runs.
t=conn     "connecting..." -> "ready" in accent-hot
t=conn+400ms  Crossfade to conversation view (clear + draw main layout)

If connection fails during startup, skip the "ready" state and go directly to the error state with the full layout showing an error message in the conversation area.

docs.title: 14.3 Message Arrival Animation
docs.text: When a new message block arrives in the conversation viewport (any role), the block appears instantly at the bottom — no slide-in animation, as Ratatui cannot animate position. However, if the viewport was auto-scrolled and a new message pushes existing messages up, the scroll_offset animation (Section 7.4) smooths the transition over 3 render ticks.

docs.title: 14.4 Animation State in App
docs.text:
The App struct needs an AnimationState sub-struct:

AnimationState {
    tick_count: u64           -- increments on every 100ms tick
    cursor_visible: bool      -- toggled every 5 ticks (500ms)
    spinner_frame: u8         -- tick_count % 8
    dot_frame: u8             -- tick_count % 6 (at 300ms rate = every 3 ticks)
    splash_phase: SplashPhase -- enum tracking startup sequence
}

The renderer reads from AnimationState — it does not produce side effects. AnimationState is updated in the tick handler, separate from the key event handler.

docs.title: 15. Screen State Inventory
docs.text: The seven mandatory screen states for each major view component:

docs.title: 15.1 Conversation Viewport
docs.text: State Trigger Visual Empty No messages, fresh session Centered welcome text: "Start by typing a message below" in text-muted Loading AppState::WaitingForResponse, no messages yet Thinking dots centered in viewport Loaded Messages present, AppState::Idle Normal message stream Error AppState::Error(_) Last message shows error block; input border in role-error Partial Very large message that exceeds viewport height Scroll indicator appears; auto-scroll still active Offline No network detected System message: "Offline — check your connection" in role-error; input disabled Refreshing User sends new message, response incoming Previous messages stay; new streaming message appended

docs.title: 15.2 Input Area
docs.text: State Trigger Visual Empty Buffer empty, idle Sigil + blinking cursor + hint line below Loading AppState::WaitingForResponse "thinking" + spinner; input disabled; border surface-border Loaded Buffer has text, idle Sigil + text + blinking cursor; border surface-focus Error AppState::Error(_) after Done Border role-error; error hint below Partial Autocomplete dropdown open Dropdown rendered above; input shows partial command Offline No network Input disabled; hint: "Offline — cannot send" Refreshing Submission accepted, clearing buffer Buffer clears; transitions to Loading state

docs.title: 15.3 File Preview Panel (split layout only)
docs.text: Documented in Section 12.1.

docs.title: 15.4 Status Bar
docs.text: State Trigger Visual Empty No model set, no cost Model slot shows "no model" in text-muted Loading Session initializing Model slot shows spinner Loaded Normal operation Full segment layout as documented Error Agent error Cost slot shows ERR in role-error Partial Budget set, >80% consumed Cost in budget-high; sparkline in budget-high Offline No network Rightmost slot shows "offline" in role-error Refreshing Tool call running Rightmost slot shows active tool name + spinner

docs.title: 16.1 Color Blindness
docs.text:
Hone's primary accent is red/pink — a problematic color for deuteranopia (red-green color blindness). The following compensating design decisions are in place:

  • Role labels are text, not color-only. The user can always read "user", "model", "tool:" as text. Color reinforces but does not replace the label.
  • The > and ! sigil prefixes (also text, not color-only) provide a secondary shape-based cue for user vs. error messages.
  • Diff + / - characters are present in the gutter — removing color still leaves the + / - text as the primary indicator.
  • The neon theme has higher contrast between all role colors, which helps users with reduced contrast sensitivity.

A future --theme colorblind preset should shift the assistant accent from pink to orange (#FB923C, ANSI 214) and preserve all other behaviors. This is not in scope for v1 but the token architecture makes it a single-struct change.

docs.title: 16.2 No-Color Mode
docs.text:
Activation conditions (checked in priority order): 1. NO_COLOR environment variable set to any value 2. TERM=dumb 3. COLORTERM not set and TERM does not contain 256color or truecolor 4. --no-color CLI flag

When no-color mode activates, the Theme struct is replaced with the Minimal theme (Section 3.4). The TUI still uses box-drawing characters and bold/underline modifiers, which work on all terminals that support the basic VT100 modifier set.

docs.title: 16.3 Keyboard-Only Navigation
docs.text:
All interactive elements are reachable by keyboard:

  • Tab cycles focus: Conversation viewport -> Input area -> File preview (if open) -> Conversation viewport.
  • Within each area, arrow keys navigate the focused element's content.
  • Enter activates the focused element's primary action.
  • Escape cancels modals (autocomplete, help overlay, approval prompt).

There is no mouse support in v1. The crossterm backend supports mouse events, but implementing mouse semantics cleanly for a streamed conversation view has high complexity for low user benefit in a terminal-first product.

docs.title: 16.4 Minimum Terminal Support
docs.text: Terminal capability Required Fallback behavior 8 ANSI colors Yes Hard minimum — Minimal theme uses bold/underline only 256-color Recommended All ANSI-256 values from the token table apply Truecolor (24-bit) Optional Hex values used when COLORTERM=truecolor; 256 otherwise UTF-8 encoding Required Box-drawing depends on UTF-8; ASCII fallback for box chars if needed Alternate screen Recommended Without it, Ratatui output will not clear on exit Bracketed paste Optional Without it, paste detection is approximate

docs.title: 16.5 Resize Handling
docs.text: The terminal emits a Resize(width, height) event via crossterm. On receipt: - Recompute all layout constraints immediately. - If the new size is below the minimum (80×24), render the too-small warning overlay. - Do not lose conversation history on resize — only the viewport render changes. - The input buffer is preserved across resize events. - Animated states reset their frame counter on resize to avoid visual glitches from mid-animation redraws.

docs.title: 17.1 Recommended Widget Assignments
docs.text: UI element Ratatui widget Notes Header bar Paragraph Manually composed Line with Spans for each color segment Conversation viewport List or custom StatefulWidget List for simple cases; custom widget for streaming cursor and tool blocks User message border Block with Borders::ALL, rounded border set Use block.border_type(BorderType::Rounded) Code block Block + Paragraph inside Nested block. Use Padding::new(2, 2, 0, 0) for horizontal pad Diff block Block + custom Paragraph Each line rendered as Line with per-span Style Tool call block Custom StatefulWidget Owns collapsed/expanded state, approval interaction Input area Paragraph with Block Update border style based on AppState Autocomplete dropdown List with ListState Positioned with Layout::split — allocate rows above input Status bar Paragraph Single Line with Spans; no border, raw background color Help overlay Clear + Block + Paragraph Clear widget paints the overlay region before the block Splash screen Custom widget Manages per-row reveal state, reads from AnimationState File preview Paragraph with line highlighting Use Style modifiers on specific Line indices Budget sparkline Inline Span sequence Composed as part of the status bar Line

docs.title: 17.2 Layout Computation
docs.text:
Use Layout::vertical and Layout::horizontal with Constraint values:

Vertical layout (single pane):
  [0] Header:   Constraint::Length(1)
  [1] Viewport: Constraint::Fill(1)
  [2] Input:    Constraint::Max(10)      -- expands up to 10, minimum 3
  [3] Status:   Constraint::Length(1)

Vertical layout (with tool panel):
  [0] Header:   Constraint::Length(1)
  [1] Viewport: Constraint::Fill(1)
  [2] Tools:    Constraint::Length(8)
  [3] Input:    Constraint::Max(7)
  [4] Status:   Constraint::Length(1)

Horizontal layout (split pane):
  [0] Left:     Constraint::Percentage(split_ratio)
  [1] Right:    Constraint::Fill(1)

split_ratio is a u16 in [30, 70], default 50. Stored in App.

docs.title: 17.3 The Message Renderer
docs.text:
The conversation viewport requires a custom rendering pass because: - Tool call blocks have interactive state (collapsed/expanded). - Code blocks have syntax-highlighted spans. - Streaming messages have animated cursors. - The viewport must scroll as a unit while individual blocks may themselves be taller than the viewport.

Recommended approach: implement a ConversationWidget that implements StatefulWidget<State = ConversationState>. The state holds: - scroll_offset: u16 — rows scrolled from the bottom - focused_block: Option<usize> — which message block has Tab focus - animation: AnimationState — reference or copy for rendering

The widget's render() method: 1. Computes the render height of each DisplayMessage in the messages slice (pre-layout pass). 2. Determines which messages are visible given scroll_offset and viewport height. 3. Renders each visible message block from bottom to top. 4. Applies the streaming cursor to the last message if is_streaming.

Pre-computing render height avoids the need to re-render off-screen messages. Cache this computation in ConversationState and invalidate it when messages change.

docs.title: 18.1 Extended Theme Struct
docs.text:
The existing Theme struct must be extended to cover all the tokens defined in Section 2.1. The full struct definition (as a spec, not code) should include:

Surface colors: - surface_base: Color — terminal background assumption - surface_raised: Color — panel fills - surface_overlay: Color — tool call, code block fills - surface_border: Color — inactive borders - surface_focus: Color — active/focused borders

Text colors: - text_primary: Color - text_secondary: Color - text_muted: Color - text_on_accent: Color

Role colors (replaces the current per-role fields): - role_user: Color - role_assistant: Color - role_system: Color - role_tool: Color - role_tool_result: Color - role_error: Color

Accent colors: - accent_hot: Color - accent_mid: Color - accent_deep: Color

Syntax colors: - syntax_keyword: Color - syntax_string: Color - syntax_number: Color - syntax_comment: Color - syntax_type: Color - syntax_function: Color

Diff colors: - diff_add_bg: Color - diff_add_fg: Color - diff_remove_bg: Color - diff_remove_fg: Color - diff_hunk_bg: Color - diff_hunk_fg: Color

Budget colors: - budget_low: Color - budget_mid: Color - budget_high: Color

Behavioral flags: - no_color: bool - use_truecolor: bool

docs.title: 18.2 Theme Selection at Startup
docs.text: Theme resolution order: 1. --theme <name> CLI flag 2. HONE_THEME environment variable 3. NO_COLOR environment variable (forces Minimal) 4. COLORTERM / TERM check (256-color vs. 8-color detection) 5. Default: Crimson dark
