  • Providers: Configure multiple providers in Providers Guide.
  • Tools: Use recipes with custom tools in Tools Guide.
  • Server: Trigger recipes remotely via Server Guide.

docs.title: Feature Status
docs.text:
Feature Status Notes Kernel sandbox (Landlock / Seatbelt) Available Linux 5.13+ and macOS Environment variable filtering Available Via sandbox.defaults.allow_env Audit logging Available JSON log to configurable path Memory encryption (AES-256-GCM) Available Requires --features encrypted-memory SQLite at-rest encryption (sqlcipher) Planned Not yet implemented

Hone implements defense-in-depth security using kernel sandboxing, network policies, and audit logging. This guide covers the sandbox architecture, threat model, and how to configure security policies.

docs.title: Linux Landlock Sandbox
docs.text:
On Linux kernel 5.13+, Hone enforces filesystem access via the Landlock LSM (Linux Security Module). The sandbox is configured per-tool using fine-grained access rules.

use hone_sandbox::{SandboxPolicyBuilder, SandboxMode};
use std::path::PathBuf;

let policy = SandboxPolicyBuilder::new(SandboxMode::Manual)
    .allow_read(PathBuf::from("/tmp"))
    .allow_write(PathBuf::from("/tmp/output"))
    .build()?;

When a tool runs a subprocess, Landlock is applied via pre_exec() so the child cannot access files outside the policy:

# If tool reads /etc/passwd (not in allow_read)
Agent calls: read_file(path="/etc/passwd")
error: Permission denied (EACCES)

Requirements: - Linux kernel 5.13+ (Landlock upstreamed in this release) - Check kernel support: cat /proc/sys/kernel/landlock/abi_version - Output >= 1 means Landlock is available - No output or error means unavailable

If Landlock is unavailable, SandboxError::Unavailable is returned and the operation is aborted (fail-closed design):

error: Landlock not available on this kernel (< 5.13)
Set [sandbox] enforce = false to disable sandboxing (not recommended).

To require Landlock and fail if unavailable:

[sandbox]
enforce = true  # fail if Landlock not available
platform = "landlock"

docs.title: Sandbox Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    Agent["Agent executes tool"]

    subgraph Platform["Platform-Specific Sandbox"]
        direction LR
        macOS["macOS: Seatbelt<br/>(sandbox_init)"]
        Linux["Linux: Landlock +<br/>seccomp-BPF"]
        Container["Container: seccomp +<br/>no-new-privs"]
        Fallback["Fallback: setrlimit +<br/>capabilities drop"]
    end

    Policy["SandboxPolicy<br/>- allow_read<br/>- allow_write<br/>- allow_exec<br/>- allow_network<br/>- allow_env"]

    Agent -->|SandboxPolicy| Platform
    Policy -->|enforced by| Platform
    Platform -->|success| Exec["Tool Executes<br/>Sandboxed"]
    Platform -->|failure| Fail["FAIL-CLOSED<br/>Operation Aborted"]

docs.title: Sandbox Platform Matrix
docs.text:
Platform Primary Fallback Notes macOS 10.5+ Seatbelt setrlimit + no-new-privs Mature, production-ready Linux 5.13+ Landlock seccomp-BPF + setrlimit Modern, fine-grained Linux <5.13 seccomp-BPF setrlimit + no-new-privs Older kernels Container seccomp + no-new-privs setrlimit Already sandboxed at OS level Windows Job Objects Restricted token Future implementation

Fail-closed invariant: If the desired sandbox tier is unavailable and required by policy, the operation aborts with SandboxError::PolicyNotMet. There is no silent downgrade.

docs.title: SandboxPolicy
docs.text:
Define what each tool call is allowed to do:

pub struct SandboxPolicy {
    pub allow_read: Vec<PathBuf>,      // paths readable by tool
    pub allow_write: Vec<PathBuf>,     // paths writable by tool
    pub allow_exec: Vec<PathBuf>,      // executables callable from tool
    pub allow_network: bool,            // network access (deny by default)
    pub allow_env: Vec<String>,        // env vars exposed to tool
}

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Sandbox policies are configured in ~/.config/hone/config.toml:

[sandbox]
platform = "auto"  # auto-detect: seatbelt, landlock, seccomp, fallback

# Default policy for all tools
[sandbox.defaults]
allow_network = false  # network deny-by-default
allow_write = ["/tmp"]  # only temp writable
allow_env = ["PATH", "HOME"]  # only safe env vars

# Per-tool policies (override defaults)
[sandbox.tools.shell]
allow_read = ["{project_root}", "/usr/lib"]
allow_write = ["/tmp", "{project_root}/target"]
allow_exec = ["/bin", "/usr/bin"]
allow_network = false
allow_env = ["PATH", "HOME", "RUST_BACKTRACE"]

[sandbox.tools.git]
allow_read = ["{project_root}"]
allow_write = ["{project_root}"]
allow_exec = ["/usr/bin/git"]
allow_network = false
allow_env = ["GIT_AUTHOR_NAME", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"]

[sandbox.tools.semantic_search]
allow_network = true  # needs network to PostgreSQL
allow_read = ["{project_root}"]
allow_env = ["DATABASE_URL"]

Variables: - {project_root} — expands to current working directory - {home} — expands to user's home directory

docs.title: Network Policy (Deny-by-Default)
docs.text:
Network access is disabled by default for all tools. Enable explicitly for specific tools that need it:

[sandbox.tools.github_api]
allow_network = true  # allow for GitHub MCP

[sandbox.tools.semantic_index]
allow_network = true  # allow for PostgreSQL

# Block everything else
[sandbox.defaults]
allow_network = false

DNS and HTTP requests are blocked unless explicitly allowed.

docs.title: Process Resource Limits
docs.text:
Prevent runaway processes using rlimit:

[sandbox.limits]
cpu_seconds = 30      # max 30 seconds CPU per tool call
memory_mb = 512       # max 512 MB RAM
disk_mb = 1024        # max 1 GB disk writes per turn
open_files = 1024     # max 1024 open files
subprocess_count = 10 # max 10 subprocesses

If a process exceeds limits, it is killed:

error: shell tool exceeded memory limit (512 MB)
Tool execution aborted by sandbox.

docs.title: Environment Variable Filtering
docs.text:
Only allow specific environment variables to reach tool processes:

[sandbox.defaults]
allow_env = ["PATH", "HOME", "USER", "SHELL"]

[sandbox.tools.git]
allow_env = ["PATH", "HOME", "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL"]

Attempt to access other env vars from a tool:

$ hone -i "Print ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
Agent calls: shell(cmd="echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
Output: (empty — variable not accessible)

docs.title: Read Allowlist
docs.text:
Only paths in allow_read are readable:

[sandbox.tools.file_reader]
allow_read = ["{project_root}", "/etc/passwd"]

Attempt to read a disallowed path:

Agent calls: read_file(path="/etc/shadow")
error: access denied (path not in allowlist)

docs.title: Write Allowlist
docs.text:
Only paths in allow_write are writable:

[sandbox.tools.code_generator]
allow_read = ["{project_root}"]
allow_write = ["{project_root}/generated"]

Attempt to write outside allowlist:

Agent calls: write_file(path="/etc/cron.d/malicious")
error: access denied (path not in allowlist)

docs.title: Symlink Handling
docs.text:
Symlinks are followed if both source and target are in the allowlist:

[sandbox.tools.safe_reader]
allow_read = ["{project_root}", "/tmp"]

# If /tmp/link -> /etc/passwd
Agent calls: read_file(path="/tmp/link")
error: access denied (target /etc/passwd not in allowlist)

docs.title: Executable Restrictions
docs.text:
Only approved executables can be called by shell commands:

[sandbox.tools.shell]
allow_exec = ["/usr/bin/git", "/usr/bin/cargo", "/bin/cat"]

Attempting to call a disallowed executable:

Agent calls: shell(cmd="python3 -c 'print(1)'")
error: access denied (executable /usr/bin/python3 not in allowlist)

This prevents: - Remote code execution via arbitrary commands - Access to system tools that shouldn't be called - Privilege escalation attempts

docs.title: RBAC Roles and Policies (Server Mode)
docs.text:
When using the daemon (honed), multiple users can have different permissions via role-based access control:

[rbac]
enabled = true

[[rbac.roles]]
name = "admin"
permissions = ["sessions:create", "sessions:delete", "tools:all", "mcp:all"]

[[rbac.roles]]
name = "developer"
permissions = ["sessions:create", "sessions:read", "tools:file", "tools:git", "tools:shell"]

[[rbac.roles]]
name = "viewer"
permissions = ["sessions:read", "mcp:read_only"]

[[rbac.users]]
user_id = "alice@example.com"
role = "admin"

[[rbac.users]]
user_id = "bob@example.com"
role = "developer"

[[rbac.users]]
user_id = "carol@example.com"
role = "viewer"

Permission meanings: - sessions:create — create new sessions - sessions:delete — delete sessions - tools:file — use file I/O tools - tools:git — use git tools - tools:shell — use shell tool - tools:all — use all tools - mcp:all — call any MCP server - mcp:read_only — only query tools (no mutation)

docs.title: Audit Logging
docs.text:
All tool calls, file accesses, and security events are logged:

[audit]
enabled = true
log_file = "/var/log/hone/audit.log"
log_level = "info"  # info, warn, error

Log entries (JSON format):

{
  "timestamp": "2026-04-05T14:30:45Z",
  "session_id": "sess_abc123",
  "user": "alice@example.com",
  "event": "tool_call",
  "tool": "read_file",
  "input": {"path": "/home/alice/src/main.rs"},
  "result": "success",
  "duration_ms": 2
}

{
  "timestamp": "2026-04-05T14:30:50Z",
  "session_id": "sess_abc123",
  "user": "alice@example.com",
  "event": "access_denied",
  "tool": "read_file",
  "input": {"path": "/etc/shadow"},
  "reason": "path not in allowlist",
  "policy": "sandbox.tools.file_reader.allow_read"
}

Query logs:

# All events for a session
grep "sess_abc123" /var/log/hone/audit.log | jq .

# All access denials
grep "access_denied" /var/log/hone/audit.log | jq .

# Events for a specific user
grep "alice@example.com" /var/log/hone/audit.log | jq .

docs.title: Memory Encryption (Encrypted Memory Feature)
docs.text:
Status: Available — Application-layer AES-256-GCM encryption of memory content is implemented in crates/hone-memory/src/encrypted.rs. This encrypts the content field of each memory record using a key derived from a user passphrase via Argon2id. Full SQLite file encryption via sqlcipher is not yet implemented (Planned).

Enable optional memory encryption to protect sensitive session data:

cargo build --features encrypted-memory

Configuration:

[memory]
encrypted = true
cipher = "aes256-gcm"

The encryption key is derived from a user passphrase via Argon2id:

hone --init-encryption
# Enter passphrase: ****
# Passphrase stored securely in system keychain.

Memory content (conversation history) is encrypted at rest. The SQLite file structure itself is not encrypted — for full disk encryption, use OS-level tools or ephemeral mode.

docs.title: Ephemeral Mode
docs.text:
Run a session with all data immediately discarded after completion:

hone --ephemeral
# or
hone -E

In ephemeral mode: - Session data is never persisted to disk - No memories are recorded - Cost tracking is not saved - Useful for sensitive queries

docs.title: Memory Persistence and Encryption
docs.text:
By default, session memories are stored in SQLite at ~/.local/share/hone/memory.db:

ls -la ~/.local/share/hone/
# memory.db            - session memories (content encrypted if --features encrypted-memory)
# sessions.db          - session metadata (if HONE_SESSION_DB set)

When built with --features encrypted-memory, the content field of each memory record is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being written to disk (see Memory Encryption above).

Full SQLite file encryption via sqlcipher is planned for a future release. Until then, for sensitive workloads where even encrypted content fields are insufficient, use --ephemeral to disable persistence entirely:

hone --ephemeral -i "Sensitive query"

Or clear memories manually:

rm ~/.local/share/hone/memory.db

docs.title: Threat Model Summary
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Malicious Prompt Injection"] -->|mitigated by| SB["Sandbox:<br/>no arbitrary exec<br/>without allowlist"]

    B["Supply Chain Attack<br/>on MCP Server"] -->|mitigated by| HASH["Content-addressable MCP<br/>server hashes in config"]

    C["Model Exfiltrating Data"] -->|mitigated by| NET["Network deny-by-default<br/>explicit allow-listing"]

    D["Runaway Disk Write"] -->|mitigated by| RL["rlimit FSIZE<br/>per operation"]

    E["Secret Leakage<br/>via env vars"] -->|mitigated by| ENV["Explicit env allowlist<br/>in SandboxPolicy"]

    F["Symlink Escape"] -->|mitigated by| SYM["Symlink target<br/>must be in allowlist"]

    G["Privilege Escalation"] -->|mitigated by| PRIV["no-new-privs flag<br/>capability dropping"]

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Start restrictive: Begin with minimal permissions and add as needed.
[sandbox.defaults]
allow_network = false
allow_write = []  # deny all writes by default

  1. Use allowlists, not denylists: Only permit known-safe paths and executables.

  2. Enable audit logging: Monitor what tools actually do.

[audit]
enabled = true
  1. Review MCP server hashes: Verify external tool integrity.
[[mcp_servers]]
name = "github"
command = "npx"
args = ["@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
hash = "sha256:abc123..."  # verify before running

  1. Rotate secrets regularly: If an API key is exposed, rotate it immediately.

  2. Use ephemeral mode for sensitive prompts:

hone -E -i "Analyze this sensitive document"

docs.title: Sandbox Not Available
docs.text:
error: sandbox policy not met (Seatbelt unavailable on this macOS version)

Check your platform:

rustc --print sysroot
uname -r  # Linux kernel version

Update to a supported OS version, or disable sandboxing (not recommended):

[sandbox]
enforce = false  # WARNING: disables security

docs.title: File Access Denied
docs.text:
error: access denied (path not in allowlist)

Add the path to the tool's allowlist:

[sandbox.tools.file_reader]
allow_read = ["/new/path"]

docs.title: Tool Process Killed (Resource Limit)
docs.text:
error: shell tool process killed (exceeded memory limit)

Increase the limit:

[sandbox.limits]
memory_mb = 1024  # was 512

Or optimize the tool to use less memory.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Getting started: See Getting Started to run your first session.
  • Tools: Configure tool sandboxes in Tools Guide.
  • Server: Secure the daemon in Server Guide.

docs.title: Server and Remote Access
docs.text: Hone can run as a daemon (honed) that exposes an HTTP/2 REST API with Server-Sent Events (SSE) for real-time streaming. This enables remote access, web UIs, and integration with other services.

docs.title: Starting the Daemon
docs.text:
honed --port 7777

The daemon listens on http://localhost:7777.

Configuration via config.toml:

[server]
host = "0.0.0.0"  # listen on all interfaces
port = 7777
auth_token = "your-bearer-token"  # optional auth
enable_https = true
cert_path = "/path/to/cert.pem"
key_path = "/path/to/key.pem"

Configuration via environment:

HONE_SERVER_PORT=7777 \
HONE_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN="secret" \
honed

docs.title: REST API Overview
docs.text:
The daemon provides these endpoints:

flowchart LR
    Client["Client<br/>(CLI, Web UI, Tool)"]

    subgraph API["HTTP/2 REST API"]
        Sessions["POST /sessions<br/>GET /sessions/{id}<br/>DELETE /sessions/{id}"]
        Turns["POST /sessions/{id}/turns<br/>GET /sessions/{id}/turns"]
        Events["GET /sessions/{id}/events<br/>(SSE)"]
        Health["GET /health<br/>GET /providers/health"]
    end

    Client -->|create session| Sessions
    Client -->|send prompt| Turns
    Client -->|stream events| Events
    Client -->|check status| Health

docs.title: Create Session
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:7777/sessions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{
    "model": "anthropic:claude-opus-4-5",
    "system_prompt": "You are a helpful assistant"
  }'

Response:

{
  "session_id": "sess_abc123",
  "model": "anthropic:claude-opus-4-5",
  "created_at": "2026-04-05T14:30:00Z"
}

docs.title: Get Session Info
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:7777/sessions/sess_abc123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

Response:

{
  "session_id": "sess_abc123",
  "model": "anthropic:claude-opus-4-5",
  "created_at": "2026-04-05T14:30:00Z",
  "turns_count": 5,
  "cost_usd": 0.34,
  "status": "active"
}

docs.title: Delete Session
docs.text:
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:7777/sessions/sess_abc123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

Returns 204 No Content on success.

docs.title: Send Prompt
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:7777/sessions/sess_abc123/turns \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{
    "input": "What is 2 + 2?"
  }'

Response (immediate, before streaming):

{
  "turn_id": "turn_001",
  "session_id": "sess_abc123",
  "status": "streaming"
}

The actual response streams via Server-Sent Events (see below).

docs.title: Get Turn History
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:7777/sessions/sess_abc123/turns \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

Response:

{
  "turns": [
    {
      "turn_id": "turn_001",
      "role": "user",
      "content": "What is 2 + 2?"
    },
    {
      "turn_id": "turn_001",
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "The answer is 4."
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Server-Sent Events (SSE)
docs.text:
Connect to the SSE endpoint to receive real-time streaming:

curl http://localhost:7777/sessions/sess_abc123/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

The connection stays open and receives events as they happen:

event: token
data: {"text": "The"}

event: token
data: {"text": " answer"}

event: token
data: {"text": " is"}

event: token
data: {"text": " 4"}

event: tool_call_start
data: {"id": "tool_001", "name": "shell"}

event: tool_call_end
data: {"id": "tool_001", "result": {"output": "..."}, "is_error": false}

event: done
data: {"usage": {"input_tokens": 45, "output_tokens": 12}, "cost_usd": 0.0012}

docs.title: Event Types
docs.text: Event Payload Description token {"text": string} A single token from the model tool_call_start {"id": string, "name": string} Tool call started tool_call_end {"id": string, "result": object, "is_error": bool} Tool call result done {"usage": {...}, "cost_usd": float} Turn complete error {"message": string} Error occurred

docs.title: Replaying Events
docs.text:
The SSE endpoint replays all events from the session start, allowing clients to connect late or reconstruct the conversation:

# Connect after the conversation started
curl http://localhost:7777/sessions/sess_abc123/events?from=turn_003

Only events from turn_003 onward are sent.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The daemon supports bearer token authentication. When auth_token is set in config, all requests must include it:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer your-token" http://localhost:7777/sessions

Without the header or with an incorrect token:

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error": "missing or invalid authorization"}

docs.title: Tunnel Support for Remote Access
docs.text: Access the daemon over the internet securely using a tunnel.

docs.title: Built-in Tunnel
docs.text:
Hone has built-in tunnel support (Cloudflare Tunnel, Ngrok, etc.):

honed --enable-tunnel --tunnel-provider cloudflare

The daemon prints a public URL:

Daemon started on http://localhost:7777
Tunnel: https://hone-abc123.trycloudflare.com
Share this URL to allow remote access.

Remote clients can now use:

HONE_SERVER_URL=https://hone-abc123.trycloudflare.com hone

docs.title: Manual Tunnel (Ngrok)
docs.text:
Alternatively, use Ngrok manually:

# Terminal 1: start daemon
honed

# Terminal 2: tunnel
ngrok http 7777

Ngrok gives you a public URL. Use it in the Hone client:

hone --server-url https://abc123.ngrok.io --auth-token "your-token"

docs.title: Health Checks
docs.text:
Check daemon and provider health:

curl http://localhost:7777/health

Response:

{
  "status": "healthy",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "uptime_secs": 3600,
  "sessions_active": 2
}

Check provider health:

curl http://localhost:7777/providers/health \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

Response:

{
  "providers": [
    {
      "id": "anthropic:claude-opus-4-5",
      "status": "healthy",
      "latency_ms": 42,
      "last_checked": "2026-04-05T14:30:00Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "ollama:llama2",
      "status": "healthy",
      "latency_ms": 1250
    },
    {
      "id": "openai:gpt-4o",
      "status": "rate_limited",
      "retry_after_secs": 60
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Web PWA
docs.text:
Hone includes a web-based UI (Progressive Web App) that connects to the daemon:

# Daemon starts on port 7777
honed --port 7777

# Open browser to localhost
# The PWA is served by the daemon
open http://localhost:7777

The web UI provides: - Session management - Real-time chat interface - Cost tracking - Session history - Markdown rendering

docs.title: Persistent Sessions with SQLite
docs.text:
By default, sessions are stored in memory and lost when the daemon restarts. To persist sessions across restarts, configure a SQLite database:

HONE_SESSION_DB=~/.local/share/hone/sessions.db honed

Or via config.toml:

[storage]
sessions_db = "~/.local/share/hone/sessions.db"

When HONE_SESSION_DB is set: - New sessions are persisted immediately - Sessions survive daemon restarts - Session history is queryable via the API

Without this setting, sessions live only in memory for the duration of the daemon process.

docs.title: Real Bore Tunnel
docs.text:
Hone can automatically use the Bore CLI for reverse tunneling. Bore is simpler and lighter-weight than Cloudflare Tunnel or Ngrok.

Install Bore:

cargo install bore-cli

Run the daemon — it auto-detects Bore on PATH:

honed

The daemon detects bore in PATH and uses BoreTunnelManager to spawn it as a subprocess. The tunnel URL is printed on startup:

Daemon started on http://localhost:7777
Tunnel: https://tunnel-abc123.bore.pub
Share this URL to allow remote access.

If bore is not on PATH, the daemon falls back to MockTunnelManager (local-only access). No error is thrown — tunneling is optional.

docs.title: Graceful Shutdown
docs.text:
The daemon handles SIGINT and SIGTERM gracefully, draining in-flight requests before exiting:

# Start daemon
honed

# In another terminal, send signal
kill -TERM <pid>

The daemon will: 1. Stop accepting new requests 2. Wait for in-flight requests to complete (with timeout) 3. Close all active SSE connections gracefully 4. Flush session data to disk (if persisted) 5. Exit cleanly

This ensures clients receive complete responses and no data is lost mid-operation.

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
All endpoints are rate-limited at 100 requests per minute per client (identified by X-Forwarded-For or source IP). Clients exceeding the limit receive 429 Too Many Requests.

To configure rate limiting when embedding the server in your own application:

use hone_server::AppState;

let state = AppState::default()
    .with_rate_limiter(100, std::time::Duration::from_secs(60));

docs.title: Collaborative Sessions
docs.text: The daemon supports multiple users working in the same session (experimental).

docs.title: Join Session
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:7777/sessions/sess_abc123/join \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"user_id": "user_123", "name": "Alice"}'

docs.title: Leave Session
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:7777/sessions/sess_abc123/leave \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"user_id": "user_123"}'

Collaborators see each other's prompts and the agent's responses in real-time via SSE. Useful for pair programming, code reviews, and team problem-solving.

docs.title: Daemon Configuration
docs.text:
Full config.toml example:

[server]
host = "0.0.0.0"
port = 7777
auth_token = "bearer_token_here"
enable_https = false
enable_tunnel = false

[server.tunnel]
provider = "cloudflare"
auth_token = "cf_token"

[providers.anthropic]
api_key = "sk-ant-..."

[providers.ollama]
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "github"
command = "npx"
args = ["@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
env = { GITHUB_TOKEN = "ghp_..." }

Start with custom config:

honed --config ~/.config/hone/config.toml

docs.title: Running Multiple Daemons
docs.text:
Run multiple daemons with different models for workload distribution:

# Terminal 1: fast responses
honed --port 7777 --model ollama:llama2

# Terminal 2: high quality
honed --port 7778 --model anthropic:claude-opus-4-5

# Terminal 3: budget conscious
honed --port 7779 --model openai:gpt-3.5-turbo

Route requests to different daemons based on needs:

# Fast response for simple tasks
hone --server-url http://localhost:7777 -i "Quick question"

# High quality for complex tasks
hone --server-url http://localhost:7778 -i "Analyze this complex code"

docs.title: Systemd Service
docs.text:
Run the daemon as a system service (Linux):

# /etc/systemd/system/honed.service
[Unit]
Description=Hone Agent Daemon
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=hone
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/honed --config /etc/hone/config.toml
Restart=on-failure
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Enable and start:

sudo systemctl enable honed
sudo systemctl start honed
sudo systemctl status honed

View logs:

sudo journalctl -u honed -f

docs.title: Tools and MCP Integration
docs.text: Hone's tool system is layered: native Rust tools for speed, MCP for extensibility, and Code Mode for custom orchestration. This guide explains each layer and how to use them.

docs.title: Layer Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    Agent["hone-core: Agent"]

    subgraph L3["Layer 3: Skills (HONE.md)"]
        HoneMd["HONE.md<br/>Markdown conventions<br/>Parsed at startup<br/>Zero runtime cost"]
    end

    subgraph L2["Layer 2: Native Tools (Rust, <1ms)"]
        FileIO["File I/O<br/>read, write, edit, glob"]
        Shell["Shell<br/>execute, capture"]
        Git["Git<br/>commit, branch, diff, undo"]
        LSP["LSP Bridge<br/>hover, diagnostics, actions"]
        Index["Semantic Index<br/>search code by meaning"]
    end

    subgraph L1["Layer 1: MCP (JSON-RPC, 10-100ms)"]
        GitHub["GitHub MCP"]
        Jira["Jira MCP"]
        Slack["Slack MCP"]
        DB["Database MCP"]
        Custom["Custom MCP"]
    end

    subgraph L0["Layer 0: Code Mode (Orchestration)"]
        CodeMode["Agent-generated<br/>TypeScript/Python<br/>Calls native + MCP via SDK"]
    end

    Agent --> L2
    Agent --> L1
    Agent --> L0
    Agent --> L3

docs.title: Layer 2: Native Tools
docs.text: Fastest layer. Direct Rust function calls. Built into Hone.

docs.title: File I/O
docs.text:
Read, write, edit files with glob pattern matching.

# List files matching a pattern
hone -i "Find all Python files in src/"
# Agent calls: glob(pattern="src/**/*.py")

# Read a file
hone -i "Show me main.rs"
# Agent calls: read_file(path="main.rs")

# Write a file
hone -i "Create a README with instructions"
# Agent calls: write_file(path="README.md", content="...")

# Edit a file (precise edits)
hone -i "Add error handling to line 42"
# Agent calls: edit_file(path="main.rs", line=42, replacement="...")

Schema:

{
  "read_file": {
    "properties": {
      "path": { "type": "string" }
    }
  },
  "write_file": {
    "properties": {
      "path": { "type": "string" },
      "content": { "type": "string" }
    }
  },
  "edit_file": {
    "properties": {
      "path": { "type": "string" },
      "line": { "type": "integer" },
      "replacement": { "type": "string" }
    }
  },
  "glob": {
    "properties": {
      "pattern": { "type": "string" }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Shell Execution
docs.text:
Execute shell commands and capture output.

hone -i "Run the tests and show me any failures"
# Agent calls: shell(cmd="cargo test", cwd="/project")

Schema:

{
  "shell": {
    "properties": {
      "cmd": { "type": "string", "description": "bash command" },
      "timeout_secs": { "type": "integer" }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Git Operations
docs.text:
Version control: commit, branch, diff, undo.

hone -i "Commit my changes with a message"
# Agent calls: git_commit(message="...", files=["main.rs"])

hone -i "Show me what changed"
# Agent calls: git_diff()

hone -i "Switch to feature branch"
# Agent calls: git_checkout(branch="feature/new-tool")

Available git tools: - git_status — show changed files - git_diff — show diffs - git_commit — create commit - git_branch — create/list branches - git_checkout — switch branches - git_undo — revert last commit - git_redo — reapply undone commit

docs.title: LSP Bridge
docs.text:
Language server integration for code intelligence. Hone now supports real LSP servers via stdio JSON-RPC. The StdioLspBridge auto-spawns a language server based on project type.

hone -i "What does this function do?"
# Agent calls: lsp_hover(file="main.rs", line=10, col=5)

hone -i "Show me all errors in this file"
# Agent calls: lsp_diagnostics(file="main.rs")

hone -i "Fix the type error on line 42"
# Agent calls: lsp_code_action(file="main.rs", line=42)

Supported Languages:

Language Server Detection Rust rust-analyzer Cargo.toml Python pyright-langserver pyproject.toml or requirements.txt TypeScript/JavaScript typescript-language-server package.json Go gopls go.mod

Available LSP Tools: - lsp_diagnostics(file: str) — get errors and warnings in a file - lsp_hover(file: str, line: int, col: int) — get hover information at a position - lsp_code_actions(file: str, line: int) — get available code actions

If the language server binary is not installed, Hone falls back to MockLspBridge that returns empty results — the tools are still registered but inactive:

# If rust-analyzer not found:
Agent calls: lsp_diagnostics(file="main.rs")
result: []  # empty (server not available)

Installation:

# Rust
rustup component add rust-analyzer

# Python
pip install pyright

# TypeScript/JavaScript
npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript

# Go
go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest

docs.title: Semantic Index
docs.text:
Search code by meaning (not keywords).

hone -i "Find functions that handle authentication"
# Agent calls: semantic_search(query="authentication", limit=10)

docs.title: Layer 1: MCP Integration
docs.text: Connect external tools via the Model Context Protocol (JSON-RPC over stdio).

docs.title: What is MCP?
docs.text:
MCP is a standardized protocol for language models to call external tools. Hone acts as an MCP client, spawning MCP servers as subprocesses and forwarding tool calls.

Benefits: - Plugin architecture — tools in any language - Lazy schema loading — only fetch tool definitions on first use - JSON-RPC transport — flexible, testable - Full bidirectional — tool can push data back to agent

docs.title: Configuring MCP Servers
docs.text:
In ~/.config/hone/config.toml:

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "github"
command = "npx"
args = ["@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
env = { GITHUB_TOKEN = "ghp_..." }

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "postgres"
command = "/usr/local/bin/mcp-postgres"
args = ["--connection-string", "postgresql://user:pass@localhost/db"]

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "slack"
command = "python3"
args = ["/path/to/mcp-slack-server"]
env = { SLACK_BOT_TOKEN = "xoxb-..." }

docs.title: Using MCP Tools
docs.text:
Once configured, MCP tools appear automatically in the agent's tool registry:

hone -i "Open a GitHub issue"
# Agent lists available tools:
# - github_create_issue
# - github_list_repos
# - github_add_comment
# ...agent calls: github_create_issue(repo="user/repo", title="...", body="...")

hone -i "Query the database for users"
# Agent calls: postgres_query(sql="SELECT * FROM users WHERE active=true")

hone -i "Post a message to Slack"
# Agent calls: slack_send_message(channel="general", text="...")

docs.title: Writing Custom MCP Servers
docs.text:
Create your own MCP server in any language. Here's a minimal Node.js example:

// server.js — MCP server that provides a custom "translate" tool
const readline = require("readline");

const rl = readline.createInterface({
  input: process.stdin,
  output: process.stdout,
});

const tools = [
  {
    name: "translate",
    description: "Translate text from English to another language",
    inputSchema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: {
        text: { type: "string" },
        language: { type: "string" }
      },
      required: ["text", "language"]
    }
  }
];

let messageId = 0;

rl.on("line", (line) => {
  try {
    const message = JSON.parse(line);

    if (message.method === "tools/list") {
      console.log(JSON.stringify({
        jsonrpc: "2.0",
        id: message.id,
        result: { tools }
      }));
    }

    if (message.method === "tools/call") {
      const { name, arguments: args } = message.params;
      let result = {};

      if (name === "translate") {
        // Dummy translation
        result = {
          translated: `[Translation to ${args.language}]: ${args.text}`
        };
      }

      console.log(JSON.stringify({
        jsonrpc: "2.0",
        id: message.id,
        result
      }));
    }
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(e);
  }
});

Register in config:

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "translator"
command = "node"
args = ["/path/to/server.js"]

Use it:

hone -i "Translate 'hello' to Spanish"
# Agent calls: translate(text="hello", language="Spanish")
# Output: "Hola"

docs.title: Layer 0: Code Mode
docs.text:
Advanced orchestration via agent-generated scripts. The agent generates TypeScript/Python code that calls native tools and MCP tools via SDK imports.

When to use Code Mode: - Complex multi-step workflows - Conditional logic based on tool outputs - Loops over collections - Custom aggregation of results

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
hone -i "Find all Python files, count lines of code, and report top 10 longest files"

Agent generates (pseudocode):

import { glob, readFile } from "@hone/native";
import { slack } from "@hone/mcp";

const files = await glob("**/*.py");
const results = [];

for (const file of files) {
  const content = await readFile(file);
  const lines = content.split("\n").length;
  results.push({ file, lines });
}

results.sort((a, b) => b.lines - a.lines);
const top10 = results.slice(0, 10);

await slack.send_message({
  channel: "general",
  text: `Top 10 longest Python files:\n${top10.map(r => `${r.file}: ${r.lines} lines`).join("\n")}`
});

Hone executes this generated code in a sandboxed subprocess, streaming results back.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text: Agents are specialized personas that combine tools, system prompts, and model preferences. Hone ships with 9 built-in agents and supports custom agents.

docs.title: What is an Agent?
docs.text:
An agent is defined in Markdown with YAML frontmatter:

---
name: code-reviewer
description: Expert code reviewer for quality, security, performance, and maintainability
tools: [read, grep, glob, shell]
model: sonnet
memory: "This agent specializes in code quality reviews"
sub_agents: []
---

You are a senior code reviewer. Perform systematic reviews following this process:

## Review Process

1. **Correctness** — Does the code do what it claims?
2. **Security** — SQL injection, XSS, command injection, secret leakage
3. **Performance** — Unnecessary allocations, N+1 queries, missing indexes
4. **Maintainability** — Naming clarity, function length, file length
5. **Tests** — Coverage of happy path, error paths, edge cases
6. **Style** — Consistent with codebase conventions

[Rest of system prompt...]

The YAML frontmatter defines: - name — Agent identifier (used with --agent flag) - description — One-line summary (used for discovery) - tools — List of available tools - model — Default model (e.g., "sonnet", "opus", "haiku") - memory — Optional contextual info - sub_agents — Other agents this one can delegate to

The Markdown body becomes the system prompt.

docs.title: Built-in Agents
docs.text:
Hone includes 9 pre-configured agents:

Agent Purpose code-reviewer Quality and security reviews debugger Systematic bug investigation security-auditor Vulnerability and secret scanning performance-optimizer Profiling and optimization documentation-agent API docs and architecture diagrams api-designer REST/GraphQL/gRPC design tdd-workflow Test-Driven Development coach rust-expert Rust best practices python-expert Python best practices

docs.title: Using Built-in Agents
docs.text:
# Use an agent by name
hone --agent code-reviewer -i "Review this code"

# Use an agent by searching its description
hone --agent "test-driven" -i "Implement a feature"  # finds tdd-workflow

The agent registry automatically loads built-in agents and matches descriptions to agent names.

docs.title: Creating Custom Agents
docs.text:
Define a custom agent in .hone/agents/my-agent.md:

---
name: my-custom-agent
description: My specialized agent for X
tools: [read, write, shell, grep, glob]
model: sonnet
---

You are a specialized agent for [your domain].

## Process

1. Understand the task
2. Take action
3. Verify results

[Your system prompt continues...]

Place custom agents in: - Project level: .hone/agents/*.md - User level: ~/.config/hone/agents/*.md

Custom agents override built-in agents with the same name. Load them automatically:

cd /your/project
hone --agent my-custom-agent

docs.title: Agent Registry
docs.text:
The AgentRegistry loads agents at startup:

use hone_core::agent_registry::AgentRegistry;

let mut registry = AgentRegistry::new();

// Load built-in agents
registry.load_builtins();

// Load custom agents from a directory
registry.load_from_dir(Path::new(".hone/agents"))?;

// Find an agent by name
if let Some(agent) = registry.get("code-reviewer") {
    println!("Agent: {}", agent.description);
}

// Find by description (case-insensitive)
if let Some(agent) = registry.find_by_description("test") {
    println!("Found: {}", agent.name);  // might be "tdd-workflow"
}

docs.title: Layer 3: Skills (HONE.md)
docs.text:
Markdown conventions parsed at startup. Zero runtime cost. Use this for system prompts, example workflows, and reusable prompts.

Create HONE.md in your project root:

# Project Skills

## Skill: Run Tests

When asked to run tests, always use `cargo test` and capture both stdout and stderr.
Explain any failures.

## Skill: Commit with Care

Before committing:
1. Run `cargo test`
2. Run `cargo clippy`
3. Review the diff with `git diff`
4. Ask for confirmation

## Skill: Code Review

When reviewing code:
1. Check for proper error handling
2. Verify all unwrap() calls are justified
3. Suggest better variable names
4. Test changes locally

The agent learns these conventions without token overhead — they're parsed once at startup and become part of the system prompt.

docs.title: Tool Registry and Dispatch
docs.text:
Hone maintains a registry of all available tools (L0, L1, L2, L3) and dispatches calls based on availability.

Access programmatically:

use hone_tools::ToolRegistry;

let registry = ToolRegistry::default();

// List all tools
for tool in registry.all() {
    println!("{}: {}", tool.name(), tool.description());
}

// Call a tool
let input = ToolInput::new(serde_json::json!({
    "path": "main.rs"
}));
let output = registry.get("read_file").unwrap().call(input, &ctx).await?;
println!("{}", output.into_value());

docs.title: Writing Custom Tools
docs.text:
Create a custom native tool by implementing the Tool trait:

use hone_tools::{Tool, ToolContext, ToolInput, ToolOutput, ToolError};
use async_trait::async_trait;

struct MyTool;

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for MyTool {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "my_custom_tool"
    }

    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        "A custom tool that does something special"
    }

    fn schema(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::json!({
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "input": { "type": "string" }
            },
            "required": ["input"]
        })
    }

    async fn call(
        &self,
        input: ToolInput,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<ToolOutput, ToolError> {
        let value = input.into_value();
        let text = value["input"].as_str().ok_or_else(|| {
            ToolError::InvalidInput("expected 'input' string".into())
        })?;

        // Your logic here
        let result = format!("Processed: {}", text);

        Ok(ToolOutput::new(serde_json::json!({ "result": result })))
    }
}

Add to the registry:

let mut registry = ToolRegistry::default();
registry.register(Box::new(MyTool));

docs.title: Sandboxing Tool Execution
docs.text: All tool calls are sandboxed for security. See Security Guide for details on: - Path restrictions (allow-list / deny-list) - Network policies (deny-by-default) - Environment variable filtering - Process resource limits

docs.title: 1. Fix a Bug
docs.text:
When to use: You found a bug and can describe it. The agent reads the code, identifies the root cause, applies a fix, and verifies it works.

Scenario: Your login function crashes when email is None. You want Hone to fix it without manually searching the codebase.

Terminal Demo:

$ hone "The login function crashes when email is None. Fix it."

  ✦ read_file auth.py
  ✦ grep -n "email is None" auth.py
  ✓ Found the issue at line 42: no null check before string operations

  ✎ edit_file auth.py
    - def login(email: str, password: str):
    -     user = db.find_user(email)
    + def login(email: str, password: str):
    +     if email is None:
    +         return None
    +     user = db.find_user(email)

  ❯ shell python -m pytest tests/test_auth.py::test_login -q
    1 passed in 0.2s

  Fixed. Added null check for email parameter before database lookup.

  deepseek-chat │ $0.001 │ ▓░░░░░░░░░ 12% ctx │ 3s

Step-by-Step Explanation:

  1. Understand: Hone reads auth.py to understand the login function structure
  2. Search: Uses grep to find references to the email check (or lack thereof)
  3. Identify: Recognizes the crash happens because email is used without validation
  4. Plan: Determines minimal fix: add a null check at function entry
  5. Edit: Edits the file using edit_file with the exact old and new strings
  6. Verify: Runs the test suite to confirm the fix works
  7. Report: Explains what was changed in one line

Tips and Variations:

  • Add logging: Ask Hone to "fix the crash AND add a debug log message when email is None"
  • Multiple languages: If you have Python and TypeScript files, Hone will fix both (using LSP for each language)
  • Custom test: Replace the default test with your own: "Fix the crash. Then run make test-auth"

Cost: ~$0.001-0.002 (DeepSeek V3)

docs.title: 2. Add a Feature
docs.text:
When to use: You want the agent to create a new function, endpoint, or module based on your specification.

Scenario: Add a new /health endpoint to your FastAPI app that returns {"status": "ok", "timestamp": "..."}.

Terminal Demo:

$ hone "Add a /health endpoint that returns {status: ok, timestamp: iso8601}"

  ✦ read_file app.py
  ✓ Found FastAPI app at line 12

  ✎ edit_file app.py
    + from datetime import datetime
    +
    + @app.get("/health")
    + def health_check():
    +     return {
    +         "status": "ok",
    +         "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
    +     }

  ❯ shell curl -s http://localhost:8000/health | jq .
    {
      "status": "ok",
      "timestamp": "2026-04-09T15:30:22.123456"
    }

  Added /health endpoint. Returns 200 OK with status and timestamp.

  deepseek-chat │ $0.001 │ ▓░░░░░░░░░ 12% ctx │ 4s

Step-by-Step Explanation:

  1. Read the code: Hone examines the existing FastAPI app to understand the structure
  2. Find the right location: Identifies where to add the new endpoint (typically near other routes)
  3. Write the code: Generates the endpoint function with proper imports and formatting
  4. Verify: Optionally runs a quick test (curl, pytest, etc.) to confirm it works
  5. Report: Summarizes the change

Tips and Variations:

  • Add tests: "Add a /health endpoint AND write a test for it in tests/test_health.py"
  • Dependency injection: "Add /health that uses the database connection pool to report db status"
  • Error handling: "Add /health that returns 503 if database is unreachable"
  • Documentation: "Add /health endpoint with full OpenAPI docstring"

Cost: ~$0.001-0.003 (DeepSeek V3)

docs.title: 3. Code Review
docs.text:
When to use: You want a specialist to review code for security issues, performance, or best practices.

Scenario: You have an authentication module in src/auth.py and want to check it for security vulnerabilities.

Terminal Demo:

$ hone --agent code-reviewer "Review src/auth.py for security issues"

  ✦ read_file src/auth.py
  ✦ lsp_diagnostics src/auth.py
  ✦ grep -n "secret\|password\|token" src/auth.py

  [code-reviewer] Findings:

  CRITICAL: Hardcoded secret at line 8
  - Code: SECRET_KEY = "dev-key-12345"
  - Risk: Secrets in source code exposed in git history
  - Fix: Load from environment variable via os.getenv("SECRET_KEY")

  HIGH: Plaintext password comparison at line 34
  - Code: if password == stored_password:
  - Risk: Timing attack vulnerability
  - Fix: Use constant-time comparison: secrets.compare_digest(password, stored_password)

  MEDIUM: No CSRF token validation on login form
  - Risk: Cross-site request forgery on login endpoint
  - Fix: Validate request.form['csrf_token'] against session

  Low-risk findings: 2 (see full report below)

  deepseek-chat │ $0.002 │ ▓▓░░░░░░░░ 16% ctx │ 8s

Step-by-Step Explanation:

  1. Read the code: Agent reads the authentication module
  2. Run diagnostics: Checks for type errors, imports, and common patterns
  3. Search for patterns: Greps for security-sensitive keywords (secret, password, token)
  4. Analyze: Applies security knowledge to identify vulnerabilities
  5. Report: Lists findings by severity with explanations and fixes

Tips and Variations:

  • Performance review: Use --agent performance-optimizer instead
  • Automatically fix: "Review src/auth.py for security issues AND fix the critical ones"
  • Specific focus: "Review src/auth.py focusing on password handling and token validation"

Cost: ~$0.001-0.003 (DeepSeek V3)

docs.title: 4. Explain Code
docs.text:
When to use: You encounter unfamiliar code and want the agent to walk you through what it does.

Scenario: You inherit a codebase with a complex rate limiter and want to understand how it works.

Terminal Demo:

$ hone "Explain what src/middleware/rate_limiter.rs does in detail"

  ✦ read_file src/middleware/rate_limiter.rs
  ✦ grep -n "struct\|impl\|fn " src/middleware/rate_limiter.rs

  The rate limiter implements a **sliding window counter** for per-IP request throttling.

  Key components:

  1. **RateLimiter struct** (lines 10-15)
     Stores: window_size_ms, max_requests, per_ip_counters (HashMap)
     Manages concurrent access via Arc<Mutex<>>

  2. **RateLimiter::new()** (lines 17-22)
     Constructor. Initializes empty counters map.

  3. **RateLimiter::check_limit()** (lines 24-45)
     Core logic:
     a. Get current timestamp
     b. For the requesting IP, find all requests in [now - window, now]
     c. If count < max_requests, allow and record timestamp
     d. Else, reject with 429 Too Many Requests

  4. **Cleanup** (lines 47-50)
     Removes old entries to prevent HashMap growth

  Time complexity: O(requests_per_window) per check
  Space complexity: O(unique_ips * requests_per_window)

  Common usage:
  ```
  let limiter = RateLimiter::new(window_ms: 60000, max: 100);
  match limiter.check_limit(&ip) {
      Ok(()) => next_handler(),
      Err(_) => 429_response(),
  }
  ```

  deepseek-chat │ $0.002 │ ▓▓░░░░░░░░ 16% ctx │ 5s

Step-by-Step Explanation:

  1. Read the code: Agent examines the file
  2. Extract structure: Greps for key definitions (structs, functions, types)
  3. Understand flow: Traces the logic from initialization through execution
  4. Explain patterns: Identifies algorithms (sliding window, hash table, etc.)
  5. Provide context: Gives time/space complexity and typical usage

Tips and Variations:

  • Visual diagram: "Explain src/rate_limiter.rs AND draw a diagram showing the data flow"
  • Comparison: "Explain how src/rate_limiter.rs compares to a token bucket approach"
  • Specific function: "Explain the check_limit() function in detail"
  • With examples: "Explain src/rate_limiter.rs with 2-3 code examples"

Cost: ~$0.001-0.002 (DeepSeek V3)

docs.title: Interactive Workflow Use Cases
docs.text: These use cases leverage Hone's interactive mode features: shell commands, vim keybindings, and TDD mode.

docs.title: 5. Quick Shell Access
docs.text:
When to use: You need to run shell commands without leaving the Hone session. Check build status, run tests, verify changes, explore the filesystem.

Scenario: During a coding session, you want to run cargo test to verify your changes, then run git status to see what changed, all without exiting Hone.

Terminal Demo:

> Write me a function to parse CSV files

[Agent writes code...]

> !cargo test
  running 12 tests
  test test_parse_csv ... ok
  test test_parse_csv_with_headers ... ok
  test test_empty_file ... ok
  12 passed, 0 failed

> !git status
  On branch feature/csv-parser
  Changes not staged for commit:
    modified:   src/lib.rs
    new file:   tests/test_csv.rs

  Untracked files:
    target/

> !git diff src/lib.rs | head -20
  +fn parse_csv(content: &str) -> Vec<Vec<String>> {

docs.title: 6. TDD with Auto-Test
docs.text:
When to use: Implementing a feature using Test-Driven Development. You want tests to run automatically whenever you make changes, providing instant feedback on pass/fail.

Scenario: You're implementing a binary search function. Instead of manually running tests after each edit, you activate TDD mode to auto-run tests on every change.

Terminal Demo:

> I'll implement a binary search function with TDD

> :tdd cargo test
  [TDD] watching for changes, running: cargo test

... (pause while waiting for edits) ...

> Implement binary search that returns the index or -1 if not found

[Agent edits src/lib.rs...]

[TDD] change detected: src/lib.rs — running tests...
[TDD] tests PASSED
  12 passed in 0.4s

> Add support for custom comparators

[Agent edits src/lib.rs...]

[TDD] change detected: src/lib.rs — running tests...
[TDD] tests FAILED
  test test_custom_comparator ... FAILED
  error: expected `fn(T, T) -> Ordering`, found closure

> Fix the comparator signature

[Agent edits src/lib.rs...]

[TDD] change detected: src/lib.rs — running tests...
[TDD] tests PASSED
  12 passed in 0.5s

> Now let's refactor for clarity

[Agent refactors...]

[TDD] change detected: src/lib.rs — running tests...
[TDD] tests PASSED
  12 passed in 0.4s

> :tdd off
  [TDD] watching stopped

Features:

  • Automatic file watching (300ms debounce to avoid rapid reruns)
  • Runs test command on every change
  • Displays PASS/FAIL with test output inline
  • Works with any test framework: cargo test, pytest, npm test, make test
  • Stop anytime with :tdd off

Red-Green-Refactor Workflow:

  1. Red: Write test that fails (or see implementation fail tests)
  2. Green: TDD mode shows FAILED, implement to make it pass
  3. Green: TDD mode shows PASSED, refactor safely with instant feedback
  4. Refactor: Modify code, TDD shows PASSED after each change

Tips and Variations:

  • Specific test file: :tdd pytest tests/test_binary_search.py
  • Fast feedback: :tdd cargo test --lib search (test single module)
  • With coverage: :tdd cargo tarpaulin --out Html (auto-generate coverage reports)
  • Watch source only: Configure to watch only src/ directory
  • Pause TDD temporarily: Run !cargo test manually, then resume with :tdd cargo test

Cost: No API cost (local test execution only)

docs.title: 8. TDD Workflow (Recipe Mode)
docs.text:
When to use: You want to implement a feature using Test-Driven Development: write test first (Red), then implementation (Green), then refactor (Refactor).

Scenario: Add rate limiting to an API. You want the structure enforced: test first, implementation, refactoring, verification.

Terminal Demo:

$ hone --recipe tdd-feature

Hone TDD Recipe
===============

What feature do you want to implement? 
> Add rate limiting to the /api/data endpoint (max 10 requests per minute per IP)

Step 1 of 4: Write the test [RED]
========================================

✎ write_file tests/test_rate_limit.py
   + def test_rate_limit_enforced():
   +     client = TestClient(app)
   +     ip = "192.168.1.1"
   +     
   +     # First 10 requests should succeed
   +     for i in range(10):
   +         resp = client.get("/api/data", headers={"X-Forwarded-For": ip})
   +         assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Request {i+1} should succeed"
   +     
   +     # 11th request should be rate limited
   +     resp = client.get("/api/data", headers={"X-Forwarded-For": ip})
   +     assert resp.status_code == 429, "Request 11 should be rate limited"

❯ shell pytest tests/test_rate_limit.py -q
  FAILED tests/test_rate_limit.py::test_rate_limit_enforced - AttributeError: 'app' has no rate limiter

✓ TEST FAILED (expected)


Step 2 of 4: Implement the feature [GREEN]
===========================================

✎ edit_file app.py
   + from ratelimit import RateLimiter
   + 
   + limiter = RateLimiter(max_requests=10, window_seconds=60)
   + 
   + @app.get("/api/data")
   + async def get_data(request: Request):
   +     if not limiter.check(request.client.host):
   +         raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail="Rate limited")
   +     return {"data": [...]}

❯ shell pytest tests/test_rate_limit.py -q
  1 passed in 0.3s

✓ TEST PASSED


Step 3 of 4: Refactor for quality [REFACTOR]
==============================================

✎ edit_file app.py
   - limiter = RateLimiter(max_requests=10, window_seconds=60)
   + limiter = RateLimiter(
   +     max_requests=10,
   +     window_seconds=60,
   +     key_func=lambda r: r.headers.get("X-Forwarded-For", r.client.host)
   + )

❯ shell pytest tests/test_rate_limit.py -q
  1 passed in 0.3s

✓ TESTS STILL PASSING


Step 4 of 4: Verify full test suite [VERIFY]
=============================================

❯ shell pytest tests/ -q
  15 passed in 1.2s

✓ ALL TESTS PASS

TDD workflow complete. Feature implemented with test coverage.

deepseek-chat │ $0.005 │ ▓▓▓░░░░░░░ 24% ctx │ 18s

Step-by-Step Explanation:

  1. RED phase: Agent writes a failing test that specifies the desired behavior
  2. GREEN phase: Agent implements the minimal code to make the test pass
  3. REFACTOR phase: Agent improves code quality without changing behavior
  4. VERIFY phase: Agent runs the full test suite to ensure no regressions

Tips and Variations:

  • Skip refactor: "Use tdd-feature but skip the refactor phase"
  • Multiple tests: "Implement feature X with at least 5 test cases"
  • Integration test: Include end-to-end tests alongside unit tests
  • With documentation: "After TDD, add API documentation to the endpoint"

docs.title: 12. Multi-Agent Orchestration
docs.text:
When to use: You have a complex task that benefits from decomposition. The orchestrator breaks it into subtasks, workers execute them in parallel, and results are merged.

Scenario: Implement user authentication with JWT tokens. This involves: backend token generation, frontend integration, token refresh logic, and security review.

Terminal Demo:

$ hone --orchestrate "Implement user authentication with JWT tokens"

  [orchestrator] Decomposing task...

  Subtasks:
  1. auth-backend: Implement JWT generation and validation in Python
  2. auth-frontend: Add login form and token storage in TypeScript
  3. refresh-logic: Implement token refresh with sliding expiration
  4. security-review: Audit the implementation for vulnerabilities

  [orchestrator] Spawning 4 workers...
  =====================================

  [worker 1 - auth-backend] Running
  ✦ read_file app.py
  ✎ write_file auth.py
   + import jwt
   + from datetime import datetime, timedelta
   + 
   + SECRET_KEY = os.getenv("JWT_SECRET")
   + TOKEN_EXPIRY_HOURS = 1
   + 
   + def generate_token(user_id: str) -> str:
   +     payload = {
   +         "user_id": user_id,
   +         "exp": datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(hours=TOKEN_EXPIRY_HOURS)
   +     }
   +     return jwt.encode(payload, SECRET_KEY, algorithm="HS256")
   + 
   + def verify_token(token: str) -> Optional[str]:
   +     try:
   +         payload = jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=["HS256"])
   +         return payload["user_id"]
   +     except jwt.ExpiredSignatureError:
   +         return None

  [worker 2 - auth-frontend] Running
  ✎ write_file src/components/LoginForm.tsx
   + export function LoginForm() {
   +     const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
   +     const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
   +     
   +     const handleLogin = async () => {
   +         const res = await fetch("/api/login", {
   +             method: "POST",
   +             body: JSON.stringify({ email, password })
   +         });
   +         const { token } = await res.json();
   +         localStorage.setItem("auth_token", token);
   +     };
   +     
   +     return (
   +         <form onSubmit={handleLogin}>
   +             <input value={email} onChange={e => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
   +             <input type="password" value={password} onChange={e => setPassword(e.target.value)} />
   +             <button type="submit">Login</button>
   +         </form>
   +     );
   + }

  [worker 3 - refresh-logic] Running
  ✎ edit_file auth.py
   + REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY_DAYS = 7
   + 
   + def generate_refresh_token(user_id: str) -> str:
   +     payload = {
   +         "user_id": user_id,
   +         "type": "refresh",
   +         "exp": datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(days=REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY_DAYS)
   +     }
   +     return jwt.encode(payload, SECRET_KEY, algorithm="HS256")
   + 
   + @app.post("/api/refresh")
   + def refresh_token_endpoint(refresh_token: str):
   +     user_id = verify_token(refresh_token)
   +     if not user_id:
   +         raise HTTPException(status_code=401)
   +     return {"token": generate_token(user_id)}

  [worker 4 - security-review] Running
  ✦ read_file auth.py
  ✓ CRITICAL: TOKEN NOT VALIDATED ON EVERY REQUEST
    Fix: Add middleware to check Authorization: Bearer <token>
  ✓ HIGH: REFRESH TOKEN SAME ALGORITHM AS ACCESS TOKEN
    Risk: Attacker can use refresh token as access token
    Fix: Sign refresh token with different key or add "type" claim
  ✓ MEDIUM: NO LOGOUT ENDPOINT
    Risk: Tokens cannot be revoked early
    Fix: Add token blacklist (Redis set)

  [orchestrator] Merging results...

  ✎ edit_file app.py
   + from functools import wraps
   + 
   + def require_auth(f):
   +     @wraps(f)
   +     def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
   +         token = request.headers.get("Authorization", "").replace("Bearer ", "")
   +         user_id = verify_token(token)
   +         if not user_id:
   +             raise HTTPException(status_code=401)
   +         return f(*args, user_id=user_id, **kwargs)
   +     return wrapper
   + 
   + @app.get("/api/protected")
   + @require_auth
   + def protected_endpoint(user_id: str):
   +     return {"user_id": user_id}

  ❯ shell pytest tests/test_auth.py -q
    12 passed in 0.8s

  Authentication system implemented:
  - Backend: JWT generation and validation with 1-hour expiry
  - Frontend: Login form stores token in localStorage
  - Refresh: Sliding token refresh with 7-day refresh token
  - Security: Middleware validates tokens on protected endpoints, separate refresh token key

Step-by-Step Explanation:

  1. Orchestrator reads the task: Understands the requirements
  2. Decompose: Breaks into 4 logical subtasks (backend, frontend, refresh, security)
  3. Spawn workers: 4 agents run in parallel on their subtasks
  4. Merge results: Lead agent integrates results, applies security fixes, runs tests
  5. Report: Summarizes what was implemented

Tips and Variations:

  • Longer orchestrations: "Build a complete user management system: auth, profiles, RBAC, audit logging"
  • Multi-language: "Implement API pagination in Go backend and React frontend"
  • Cross-cutting: "Add comprehensive logging to all services"
